title: Hannon Act #1 (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Hannon Act #1 (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The 2020 Hannon Act requires VA to submit an annual report on the Fox Grant program.

I hereby request the following records: a copy of the 2026 report. (For reference, I can attach a copy of the 2025 report, which includes data up until March of 2025. Just let me know.)

If such a report does not exist, I am requesting a copy of raw data that was tabulated on the Fox Grant Program, including:

•	The total number of (a) veterans, (b) service members and (c) family members who entered the Fox Grant Program in 2025
•	The total number of (a) veterans, (b) service members and (c) family members who entered the Fox Grant Program and for whom an entry baseline mental health assessment was conducted in 2025.
•	The total number of individuals who were in the program on January 1, 2025.
•	The total number of individuals who were in the program on December 31, 2025.
•	The total number of individuals who exited the program during the calendar year.
•	The total number of individuals who exited the program during the calendar year and for whom a mental health assessment was conducted and data forwarded to the VA.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jasper Craven

communications.communication:

communications.subject: RE: Washington Public Records Act Request #W038325-072226
communications.communication:
Hello,

In your previous communication, you indicated that if I have filed multiple requests, you may wait until the first request is completed before starting to process the next one.

Please be advised of that in the recent ruling in Seattle Times v. City of Seattle (2026), the King County Superior Court ruled that "nothing in the PRA or in caselaw interpreting the PRA supports the notion that a single request should have a lower agency priority simply because it was made by a person who has other pending requests" and that "making public records requests, even voluminous public records requests, is not by itself an unreasonably disruptive or disrespectful act" (referring to  WAC 44-14-01002) and thus ", SPD’s
implementation of MDAR 17-0002 § 5.2.1 [a policy where requests were similarly grouped by requester] does not facilitate timely access to public records and is contrary to law."

I ask that you please confirm that my request is not being unlawfully queued.

Thank you,
Rose

title: Sheriff use of force data (2017-2025) under 50k population (Jefferson County Sheriff)

communications.subject: Wisconsin Open Records Act Request: Sheriff use of force data (2017-2025) under 50k population (Jefferson County Sheriff)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Use of force (UOF) data dating from January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2025. If possible, please provide this data in database or spreadsheet format and include the case number, incident date, incident time, subject injured indicator, subject injury force related info (e.g. Yes or No), subject age, subject gender, subject ethnicity, subject weapon type, incident area occurred, force type, officer division (e.g. law enforcement operations, detention/correctional operations, etc.), badge number and names associated with the officers involved. If one or more of these fields is unavailable, provide all fields and/or information that is available responsive to my request. If no database or spreadsheet format is available, please provide copies of each individual use of force report or other report where use of force information is documented/reported by officers. Note, this is for all use of force incidents reported by your agency, not limited to only those incidents required to be reported under state or federal programs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Samuel Sinyangwe

title: Request for Lexipol correspondence (Hayward Police Department)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Request for Lexipol correspondence (Hayward Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All records, between the Department and the company Lexipol  (lexipol.com) or its representatives that contain any references to “military equipment” or “AB 481”, including documents, emails and attachments, texts, spreadsheets, recordings, memoranda, and other materials, from July 1, 2024 to the present. 

Records on the Department’s web site indicate that it has used Lexipol templates for at least some policies. 

To assist with the prompt release of responsive material, I ask that you make records available to me as you locate them, rather than waiting until all responsive records have been collected and copied.
 
This request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

John Lindsay-Poland

title: Case management system procurement records – Journal Technologies (AODA)

communications.subject: New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act Request: Case management system procurement records – Journal Technologies (AODA)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Electronic copies of the following existing public records concerning the procurement of a case management system from Journal Technologies, Inc. by the Administrative Office of the District Attorneys, including the FY2026 purchase orders described in state records as "Off the shelf case management system" (approximately $2,325,928 and $800,000):

1. The solicitation document(s) used for this procurement — the Request for Proposals, Invitation to Bid, sole-source determination and posting, or the statewide/cooperative price agreement relied upon — including any addenda and written questions and answers.

2. All proposals, bids, or quotes received in response, including the proposal submitted by Journal Technologies, Inc., with any price schedules or cost proposals.

3. The evaluation committee's scoring sheets, tabulations, and any written evaluation summary or recommendation of award.

4. The notice of award or intent to award, and any protest filed and its resolution.

5. The executed contract or agreement with Journal Technologies, Inc., including all exhibits, statements of work, deliverable and payment schedules, license or subscription terms, service-level terms, and all amendments to date.

6. Any Project Certification Committee (DoIT) certification request forms, project charters, or project management plans submitted for this project.

7. Any implementation schedule, rollout plan, or memorandum identifying which district attorney offices are onboarded to the system and on what dates.

I do not require the compilation of new records; existing records only. Electronic copies (PDF or native format) are requested. Please advise of any fees before incurring them.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

cassy

title: Flock NightShift OS Investigate Dunwoody PD

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock NightShift OS Investigate Dunwoody PD
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request follows an August 19, 2026 WIRED investigation, “Flock Has a Powerful New AI Tool for Police. We Got Its Code,” by Dhruv Mehrotra and Dell Cameron, describing an AI-powered investigative tool built by Flock Safety, referred to internally as “Nightshift” and more recently as “OS Investigate.” According to that reporting, the tool is being piloted with a small group of law enforcement partners and provides natural-language search across license-plate data, case files, dispatch logs, arrest records, and commercial databases, using 69 prewritten prompts and 45 distinct tools.
Records reviewed by the requester indicate that DPD is among the agencies with Nightshift access. Specifically, an organization-level event log entry attributed to Martin Howley, dated October 10, 2025, records the setting “Can Use Nightshift” being changed from “Disabled” to “Enabled” for the Dunwoody Police Department account. A subsequent DPD search-audit export covering October 1–31, 2025 shows at least six Nightshift searches run on October 15, 2025 by Patrick Krieg, each categorized under the case label “Night Shift Case” and the stated reason “convoy,” querying vehicle records in Georgia and Indiana (audit record identifiers a70f3c10-55a1-48d3-92bf-b065cc809dfd, 622e30aa-1417-4390-af51-2da46f68c1e2, 4a75d6ff-edcf-43c5-a71c-7896ca78f4de, 8ff746b8-c1d8-4108-8e98-0ce4869d4d43, 4c679569-b155-4ed0-aaf7-f9ae226d2c23, and 4c6fb005-7af0-42be-aec9-684c36d86c2b). This request is not limited to those records, but they are cited to establish that DPD holds responsive records and to identify specific entries within DPD’s possession.
Accordingly, I request the following records, in any format (electronic preferred), for the period January 1, 2024 through the date this request is processed:
1.	All prewritten, preloaded, or template prompts associated with Nightshift/OS Investigate, including but not limited to the set of approximately 69 prompts referenced in the WIRED article.
2.	Any documentation, manuals, specification sheets, or internal guides describing the tools, data sources, or integrations available to Nightshift/OS Investigate (including the approximately 45 “tools” referenced in the article), such as what databases, camera networks, case management systems, dispatch systems, or commercial data providers it can query.
3.	Any policies, standard operating procedures, or general orders governing officer use of Nightshift/OS Investigate, including any requirements for documenting a search justification, case number, or supervisory approval.
4.	Training materials, presentations, or onboarding documents provided to DPD personnel regarding Nightshift/OS Investigate.
5.	Any audit logs, usage logs, or search logs generated by DPD personnel’s use of Nightshift/OS Investigate, including the stated reason or justification and case number (if any) associated with each search.
6.	All records associated with the “Night Shift Case” label applied to the Nightshift searches DPD personnel ran on October 15, 2025 (audit record identifiers a70f3c10-55a1-48d3-92bf-b065cc809dfd, 622e30aa-1417-4390-af51-2da46f68c1e2, 4a75d6ff-edcf-43c5-a71c-7896ca78f4de, 8ff746b8-c1d8-4108-8e98-0ce4869d4d43, 4c679569-b155-4ed0-aaf7-f9ae226d2c23, and 4c6fb005-7af0-42be-aec9-684c36d86c2b), including any underlying incident report, case number, or offense associated with the stated reason “convoy,” and identification of the vehicles, plates, or individuals returned by those searches.
7.	The complete Nightshift/OS Investigate audit or search-log export for DPD’s account from October 1, 2025 to the date this request is processed, including every user, search reason, case label, case number, and state or jurisdiction queried.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

I hereby request the following records: 1. Justification Records All records used to justify adoption of Flock Safety cameras, including but not limited to: staff reports, city council or county board memoranda, crime analysis reports, presentations, vendor proposals, and any other documents that described the purpose, anticipated benefit, or stated rationale for purchasing or leasing the system. 
2. Effectiveness and Use Statistics All statistical reports, internal summaries, use-justification documents, crime-reduction assessments, or after-action reviews evaluating the effectiveness of Flock Safety cameras since installation. This includes any records prepared in connection with contract renewals. 
3. Cost and Financial Records All financial records related to Flock Safety cameras, including invoices, purchase orders, annual subscription payments, installation costs, and maintenance costs from the date of first installation through the present. Include any records showing federal, state, grant, or civil asset forfeiture funding used to offset costs. 
4. Camera Inventory and Placement The current inventory or deployment list of Flock Safety cameras operated by or accessible to this agency, including number of units and general location descriptions. Also include any written policies, criteria, risk assessments, or internal documents used to determine camera placement locations. 
5. Contracts and Legal Agreements Copies of all active and recently expired contracts, amendments, renewals, data-sharing agreements, memoranda of understanding, and scope-of-work documents between this agency and Flock Safety. 
6. Data Access and Network Sharing (a) The Flock "Organization Audit" report showing all searches made within this agency's Flock system from the date of installation through the date of this request. (b) The Flock "Network Audit" report showing all searches of this agency's Flock data by any outside agency from the date of installation through the date of this request. (c) A list of all agencies currently authorized to access this agency's Flock data, including any federal agencies. Please provide these records in their original electronic, machine-readable format (CSV or spreadsheet). 
7. Security Incidents and Unauthorized Access All records documenting any security incidents, unauthorized access, data breaches, hacking events, or unauthorized sharing of data collected by Flock Safety cameras, including any correspondence with or notifications from Flock Safety related to such incidents. 
8. Secretary of State Audit All records, correspondence, or internal communications related to the Illinois Secretary of State's 2025 audit of ALPR data-sharing practices, including any communications with the Secretary of State's office or Flock Safety regarding compliance. 
9. Marketing and Sales Materials All promotional, descriptive, and marketing materials shared with this agency by Flock Safety or any representative thereof prior to or in connection with the purchase or renewal of the Flock Safety system. 
10. Communications with Flock Safety Emails to/from Flock Safety personnel addresses; sales@flocksafety.com, support@flocksafety.com, or any email addresses in the format firstname.lastname@flocksafety.com from January 1, 2022 through the date this request is processed. If this date range is too burdensome due to the amount of emails, then I'd like it narrowed down to January 1, 2022 through December 31, 2022 & January 1, 2025 to the date this request is processed.

communications.subject: RE: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Community ALPR Audit (City Of East Peoria, Il Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Public Access Counselor:

Pursuant to Section 9.5 of the Illinois Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 ILCS 140/9.5, I hereby request review of a public body's failure to respond to a FOIA request as required under 5 ILCS 140/3.

1. Identification of Public Body

City of East Peoria Police Department
East Peoria, IL

2. Date of Original Request

I submitted the FOIA request electronically via the MuckRock platform on August 11, 2026.

3. Summary of Records Sought

The request sought ten categories of records concerning the Department's Flock Safety Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) system, including, among other things:

• Justification records for the system's adoption
• Effectiveness and use statistics
• Cost and financial records, including any grant or civil asset forfeiture funding
• Camera inventory and placement criteria
• Contracts and data-sharing agreements with Flock Safety
• The Flock "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" reports documenting searches made within and of the Department's Flock system, and a list of all outside agencies (including federal agencies) authorized to access the Department's ALPR data
• Records of any security incidents or unauthorized access to ALPR data
• Records related to the Illinois Secretary of State's 2025 audit of ALPR data-sharing practices
• Marketing materials and correspondence with Flock Safety

4. Statutory Violation
Under 5 ILCS 140/3(d), a public body must respond to a FOIA request within 5 business days of receipt, or, if a proper written extension notice citing one of the grounds enumerated in 5 ILCS 140/3(e) is provided within that period, within an additional 5 business days. As of the date of this filing, more than five (5) weeks have elapsed since the request was submitted. The Department has:

• Issued no written response, denial, extension notice, or acknowledgment of any kind;
• Failed to respond to a written follow-up inquiry sent on August 26, 2026 (Exhibit B); and
• Failed to respond to a second written follow-up inquiry sent on September 10, 2026 (Exhibit C).

The request status remains "Awaiting Acknowledgement." No fee determination, partial production, or claim of exemption has been communicated. This constitutes a clear violation of 5 ILCS 140/3(d) and, under 5 ILCS 140/9.5(a)-(b), the failure to respond is deemed a denial of the request, ripe for review by this office.

5. Timeliness of This Request for Review

This Request for Review is filed within sixty (60) days of the violation, as required by 5 ILCS 140/9.5(b).

6. Relief Requested

I respectfully request that the Public Access Counselor:

1. Open a Request for Review file and direct the City of East Peoria Police Department to respond immediately to the underlying FOIA request in full;
2. Advise the Department of its obligations under 5 ILCS 140/3 and the consequences of continued noncompliance, including potential civil penalties under 5 ILCS 140/11(j) and referral for further enforcement;
3. Specifically direct production of the Flock "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" reports (Item 6(a)-(b) of the original request) and the list of outside agencies with data access (Item 6(c)), in the native electronic/machine-readable format originally requested; and
4. Issue a binding opinion, if the Department continues to fail to respond or improperly withholds records, pursuant to 5 ILCS 140/9.5(f)-(g).

7. Link to FOIA request

• https://www.muckrock.com/foi/east-peoria-7760/community-alpr-audit-city-of-east-peoria-il-police-department-218048/

I certify that the foregoing is true and correct to the best of my knowledge.

Respectfully,
Trever Flahaut
9/17/2026

title: Johnny Novielo Death Records (Bureau of Prisons)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Johnny Novielo Death Records (Bureau of Prisons)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All records pertaining to the detention, care, death, and post-death inquiry for Johnny Noviello, (DOB: 7/1/1975; DOD: 6/25/2025), who died in ICE custody after incarceration at BOP's Federal Detention Center - Miami facility. See https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddr_NOVIELLOJohnny.pdf. 

This request includes, but is not limited to, the following records: 

1. Any Mortality Review  and associated working papers conducted by ICE Health Services Corps or the Bureau of Prisons
2. Any Death Review conducted by ICE ERAU or BOP
3. Any Healthcare and Security Compliance Analysis or similar document created by Creative Corrections or another Contractor
4. All extant video showing Mr. Noviello in ICE or BOP custody.
5. All BOP and/or ICE medical records for Mr. Noviello. 
6. Any Executive Summary or Findings information regarding Mr. Noviello's death
7. Any autopsy report for Mr. Noviello, complete with toxicology. 
8. Records of any contract discrepancy reports or similar findings.

I request expedited processing of this request pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e) and declare under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 USC 1746 that the following statements are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and understanding: 

1. I am a member of the news media investigating and reporting edited pieces on deaths in ICE custody and abuses of power by federal law enforcement agencies. See, e.g., https://theappeal.org/authors/andrew-free/. 
2. Mr. Noviello is the first ICE detainee to die in a BOP facility in over a decade. 
3. His death in BOP's FDC Miami following his imprisonment at Krome Service Processing Center has been the subject of widespread media coverage about which serious questions exist as to the care the government provided him. 
4. ICE's Miami Field Office has overseen the custody and care of at least six (6) people, including Mr. Noviello, who died in ICE custody in FY25--the most of any field office in the United States.
5. An urgent need exists for the public to obtain, review, and understand the circumstances surrounding Mr. Noviello's death in custody as ICE deaths continue to rise to their highest levels since the Covid pandemic and the agency is poised to massively expand ICE detention capacity.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

communications.subject: Public Records Request :: P066761-021826
communications.communication:
Dear Michael Michael: 
Our office received your open records request pursuant to Missouri's Sunshine Law, Chapter 610, RSMo. Your request has been assigned number P066761-021826. The Patrol is committed to adhering to the Sunshine Law and to ensuring that the public obtains access to open records that are not otherwise closed by law. The Sunshine Law requires each public agency to adhere to certain standards. This letter is designed to ensure that you understand our process for fulfilling your records request. Three Business Day Notice Requirement: 
The requested records are not immediately available for dissemination or inspection. The Patrol is required to notify you that additional research time will be required to fulfill the request. This correspondence satisfies the Sunshine Law's notice requirement within the required three business day period. Section 610.023.3, RSMo. 
 Additional Research Time is Required: 
The Patrol receives thousands of open records requests each month. Our Patrol Records Division personnel are dedicated to meeting the intent of Missouri's Sunshine Law and strive to respond to each request in a timely manner. The Patrol operates in all 114 Missouri counties and the independent city of St. Louis. Accordingly, many records maintained by the agency are not centrally located within, or immediately accessible to, the Patrol's Custodian of Records in Jefferson City. Our staff must research your request and ensure that we have captured all responsive records  ̶  regardless of their location within the agency. The research process is time-consuming, but we will make every effort to expedite your request. Estimated Time for Completion: 
The majority of our requests are fulfilled within thirty business days. Some requests require additional research time due to their scope or complexity. Our team will conduct an initial review of your request. If we estimate that the request will be fulfilled within thirty business days, we will not send an updated time estimate. However, if we estimate that the request will take longer than thirty business days, we will provide an updated time estimate that provides a detailed justification for the additional research time. Billing: 
As it relates to billing, Missouri law allows the Patrol to charge fees for copies and research time. Specifically, "[r]esearch time required for fulfilling records requests may be charged at the actual cost of research time." Section 610.026, RSMo. The Missouri Supreme Court recently determined that "staff time is the time required to provide access to public records maintained on computer facilities, recording tapes or disks, videotapes or films, pictures, maps, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items". Gross v. Parson, 624 S.W.3d 877, 884-89 (Mo. 2021) (internal quotations omitted). 
The Patrol will never bill you for redaction time or any research time conducted by our legal staff. You will only be charged for copies and staff research time as permitted by Missouri law. Please let us know if you have questions related to the billing estimate. 
Our team will forward a bill estimate to your attention once we have calculated the permissible costs and fees. The Patrol will not provide the responsive records until receipt of payment. Section 610.026.2, RSMo. 
We appreciate your patience as we review, research, and fulfill your open records request. You can monitor the progress of your request at the link below and you will receive an email when your request has been completed. If you wish to withdraw or clarify your request, or if you have questions, please call our office at (573) 526-6146, or (573) 526-6167. 
 
Sincerely, 
Gerard G. Callahan 
Custodian of Records 
 
Login Link: https://mshp.govqa.us/WEBAPP/_rs/Login.aspx

communications.communication:
Mr. Gerard Callahan,
I am very disappointed that there have been no further responses to this request.

Missouri sunshine law is very clear about time frames.  The MSHP is very careful to construct their initial response so that they can avoid the 3 business day requirement on all record responses.

However, the MSHP is not continuing to comply with sunshine law time frames.  Although production may take longer than three business days, the MSHP is required to give the earliest date AND time the records may be available (place also, but I imagine they will provided electronically).  The MSHP has not ever met this requirement on this request.

I am requesting the earliest date and time the records will be available as required by 610.023.3, which you yourself have cited.  In addition, a detailed explanation for the delays so far is required and requested.  I would like to know why the MSHP cannot provide audit procedures in the time you gave yourself, which is quite generous.

Thank you,
Michael

title: Deed Fraud Unit (ROD)

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Deed Fraud Unit (ROD)
communications.communication:
Under the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I request the following existing records maintained by the Wayne County Register of Deeds concerning the Mortgage and Deed Fraud Unit for Jan. 1, 2016 through the date this request is processed:

- Monthly, quarterly and annual statistical reports showing inquiries or complaints received, cases opened, cases referred for investigation, search warrants, arrest warrants, criminal charges, convictions, cases closed and stolen homes or properties returned.
- The existing records used to calculate or substantiate the cumulative figures currently published on the Register of Deeds’ Mortgage and Deed Fraud Unit webpage: 13,013 inquiries, 2,343 cases opened, 1,172 search warrants, 505 arrest warrants, 347 convictions and 393 stolen homes returned.

This includes any existing spreadsheet, database report, running tally, case log or statistical worksheet used to update those figures. Please provide electronic records in their native format with all existing fields and formulas intact. I am not requesting the creation of a new compilation.

- Existing definitions, written methodologies, policies or instructions explaining what the unit counts as an “inquiry,” “case opened,” “search warrant,” “arrest warrant,” “conviction” and “stolen home returned,” including whether multiple defendants or multiple properties within one investigation are counted separately.
- Records showing when the figures on the webpage were most recently updated and the figures that appeared before each update since Jan. 1, 2016.
- Existing reports showing complaints that were declined, closed without investigation or referred to another agency, including the reason categories used for those dispositions.

If a responsive record contains exempt personal or investigative information, please redact that information and produce all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions. If no responsive record exists for an item, please state that. Electronic records should be provided in their native format where available.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

Records or data sufficient to show the number of undergraduate students employed by the university as of August 5, 2026, or for the 2025–26 academic year, broken down, if such data is maintained, by:

If the university does not maintain data in the categories described above, I request the records in whatever form the data is kept, and ask that you advise me of the categories that are available.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Sincerely,

Joe Smith

title: Kissinger clearance foreign travel

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Kissinger clearance foreign travel
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

concerning Dr. Henry A. Kissinger (born May 27, 1923, Fürth, Germany; died November 29, 2023):
1.	All background investigation files (initial and periodic reinvestigations), including reports of interview, record checks, and subject interview summaries, conducted by DCSA, the National Background Investigations Bureau, OPM Federal Investigative Services, the Defense Security Service, or the Defense Investigative Service in connection with Dr. Kissinger's eligibility for access to classified information, including his service on the Defense Policy Board and any earlier DoD consulting or advisory roles.
2.	All adjudicative records, including eligibility determinations, statements of reasons, incident reports, continuous evaluation or continuous vetting alerts, and any records of self-reported or externally reported foreign travel, foreign contacts, or foreign financial interests.
3.	All entries concerning Dr. Kissinger in the Defense Central Index of Investigations (DCII), the Joint Personnel Adjudication System (JPAS), and the Defense Information System for Security (DISS), including eligibility history and incident-report history.
4.	Any record of Dr. Kissinger's security debriefing upon termination of his eligibility in or after November 2020.

Dr. Kissinger is deceased, which substantially diminishes the personal privacy interests protected by Exemptions 6 and 7(C). A copy of the obituary is attached.

If any responsive records have been transferred to another agency or to the National Archives, please identify the recipient. If any responsive records were destroyed, please state the records-disposition authority under which they were destroyed and the date of destruction.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

communications.subject: FOIA Response - Muckrock
communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Requester –

Please allow this email to acknowledge your September 17, 2026, request (“Request”) pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act (“FOIA”), 5 ILCS 140/1 et seq., received on September 17, 2026.  5 ILCS 140/3(d); 5 ILCS 140/3.5(a). On September 24 and October 1, the Office properly extended the time to respond to your request  to October 16, 2026.  5 ILCS 140/3(e).  Your Request seeks the following records:

This request covers September 1, 2025 through the date of your search. I seek all IL FOIA requests the Office has received about the Secretary of State's Plate Watch Hotline, the Office's responses, and the records released in response.

The Office has conducted a reasonably diligent search of its physical and electronic databases and has identified certain responsive records to your Request within its possession and custody.  5 ILCS 140/2(c).  The responsive record is attached with this correspondence.  However, the Office has withheld certain exempt information pursuant to applicable FOIA exemptions.  The Office’s factual basis for this denial of your request is detailed below.  5 ILCS 140/9.

The disclosure of the following information is a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy, and therefore the Office is withholding the following information:  other third-party names (Ill. Att’y Gen. PAC Req. Rev. Ltr. 31526, issued November 26, 2014, at 6). 5 ILCS 140/7(1)(c).

The Office has withheld administrative information that, if disclosed, would jeopardize the security of the email and telephone software and operating protocols.  5 ILCS 140/7(1)(o).  The Office oversees 20+ departments and 4,000+ employees.  Providing the office phones and office emails of each of the Office’s 4,000+ employees would disrupt the duly undertaken work of the Office.  5 ILCS 140/1.  See Masiarczyk v. IRS, No. 1:04CV85, 2005 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 428715 (N.D.W. Wa. Oct. 3, 2005) (“Disclosure of internal administrative information services no public benefit”); Voinche v. FBI, 46 F. Supp. 3d 26, 30 (D.D.C. 1999) (“Telephone number of the Public Corruption Unit is a trivial administrative matter of no genuine public interest”).

The Office has redacted unique identifiers, including personal license plates; home or personal telephone numbers; signatures (Ill. Att’y Gen. Pub. Acc. Op. No. 14-015, issued March 25, 2014, at 11) from the responsive record pursuant to FOIA exemption 7(1)(b), which expressly exempts private information from disclosure.  5 ILCS 140/2(c-5); 5 ILCS 140/7(1)(b).

You have the right to have any denial of your request reviewed by the Public Access Counselor (“PAC”) at the Office of the Illinois Attorney General.  5 ILCS 140/9.5(a).  You can file your Request for Review with the PAC by writing to:  Public Access Counselor, Office of the Illinois Attorney General, 500 S. 2nd St., Springfield, IL 62701, (877) 299-3642, public.access@ilag.gov.  5 ILCS 140/9.5(a).  You also have the right to seek judicial review by filing a lawsuit in the State circuit court.  5 ILCS 140/11.

Respectfully,

title: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Calvert County Sheriff's Department)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Calvert County Sheriff's Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I am hereby requesting access to the records listed below and held by the Calvert County Sheriff's Department.

1)	Any policies, procedures, protocols, and/or written guidance for the use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) by Calvert County Sheriff's Department. This request includes, but is not limited to policies setting forth permitted and prohibited uses for ALPRs and rules regarding who may and may not use this technology.

2)	Information about which people and agencies have access to images, videos, and raw data sets generated by ALPR systems monitored or maintained by Calvert County Sheriff's Department, under what circumstances these individuals have access to the above-mentioned data, and what information must be entered about any data requests. The list of agencies includes, but is not limited to, parking and traffic enforcement agencies, and other law enforcement agencies.

3)	Policies, procedures and information regarding Calvert County Sheriff's Department data retention and data purging practices for ALPR systems, including  Calvert County Sheriff's Department policies regarding handling images, videos, and raw data sets.

4)	Information about Calvert County Sheriff's Department audits or other procedures used to assure compliance with the above requirements.

5)	Information regarding the training that Calvert County Sheriff's Department personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

6)	ALPR training materials provided to Calvert County Sheriff's Department.

7)	Product and user manuals for all ALPR software and hardware possessed or used by Calvert County Sheriff's Department.

8)	The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Calvert County Sheriff's Department or by third party who make the information available to Calvert County Sheriff's Department. Hardware includes fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile devices. Software systems include optical character recognition and artificial intelligence capabilities.

9)	Description of how targets (aka “hot lists”) are shared with ALPR systems and monitored, including the sources for these data feeds.

10)	A list and map of locations where fixed-location ALPRs are currently located within Calvert County Sheriff's Department’s jurisdiction.

11)	The number of ALPR devices operated by the agency for the following categories: fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile ALPRs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, please disclose total charges in advance of fulfilling the request. Alternatively, please consider waiving any fees, pursuant to § 4-206(e)(2)(ii) of the General Provisions Article, as this request is on behalf of individuals served by the Maryland Office of the Public Defender, a state government agency, which solely serves indigent citizens of Maryland. As a result, my request for the above-listed public records is in the public interest. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Gilleran
Chief Attorney
Forensics Division
Office of the Public Defender
6 St. Paul St., Suite 1508
Baltimore, MD 21202
(410) 804-7107
jeffrey.gilleran@maryland.gov

title: Marion County, WV Opioid Settlement Funds Spring 2026

communications.subject: West Virginia Freedom of Information Act Request: Marion County, WV Opioid Settlement Funds Spring 2026
communications.communication:
Drew Solt
1511 University Avenue, P.O. Box 6010
Morgantown, WV 26506-6010
Mar. 12, 2026

200 Jackson Street
Fairmont, WV 26554

To whom it may concern,

Under the West Virginia Freedom of Information Act, §29-B-1-1 et seq., I am requesting an opportunity to inspect or obtain copies of public records that pertain to Marion County opioid settlement funds. Specifically, I am requesting:
- Documentation of the amount of funds the county has received from the federal opioid lawsuit settlements from March 1, 2025 through today
- The application forms that any organization would submit to receive settlement funds
- Documentation of how much county-level funding has been awarded from March 1, 2025 to today
- Any completed application of an organization that has received settlement funds from the county from from March 1, 2025 to today
- Documentation of the process by which funds are awarded
- Any documents that contain the names of the individuals who review the funding applications and determine the awards
- Any documents that account for future plans from the county for the use of opioid settlement funds

If there are any fees for searching or copying these records, please inform me if the cost will exceed $25. However, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees in that the disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest and will contribute significantly to the public’s understanding of how the opioid settlement funds are being spent. I am a student journalist whose request is strictly for news-gathering purposes. This information is not being sought for commercial purposes.

The West Virginia Freedom of Information Act requires a response to this request be made within five business days. If access to the records I am requesting will take longer than this amount of time, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

If you deny any or all of this request, please cite each specific exemption you feel justifies the refusal to release the information and notify me of the appeal procedures available to me under the law.
Thank you for considering my request.

Sincerely, Drew Solt
740-243-6793
drewsolt@yahoo.com

title: KING COUNTY DIRECTORS' ASSOCIATION – Board of Directors Meeting(s) Records (2026)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: KING COUNTY DIRECTORS' ASSOCIATION – Board of Directors Meeting(s) Records (2026)
communications.communication:
KING COUNTY DIRECTORS' ASSOCIATION – Board of Directors Meeting(s) Records (2026)

June 10, 2026

via email to: Kristen Deskin, Human Resources Manager and Public Records Officer <kdeskin@kcda.org>

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act [RCW 42.56], I hereby request the following records:

1. Produce copies of all "Records and Writings" of all minutes, complete meeting packets, resolutions, audio or video recordings, executive session logs, and presentations, inclusive, for every meeting of the KCDA Board of Directors for the year 2026, including all records provided to the Board by Executive Directors Bart Powelson or David Mahalko regarding litigation updates, vendor awards, or funding-out contract terminations.

DEFINITION OF RECORDS AND WRITINGS

"RECORDS AND WRITINGS" as defined by RCW 42.56.010(4): any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, and every other means of recording any form of communication or representation including, but not limited to, letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combination thereof, and all papers, maps, magnetic or paper tapes, photographic films and prints, motion picture, film and video recordings, magnetic or punched cards, discs, drums, diskettes, sound recordings, and other documents including existing data compilations from which information may be obtained or translated.

PRODUCTION PROCESSING AND DELIVERY OF ELECTRONIC RECORDS

Please provide all records in their native electronic format. Please do not instead create new records by printing electronic files then scanning and printing the newly scanned prints.

To preserve metadata and ease review, please produce as follows:

Emails: PST (Microsoft Outlook) or MBOX containers.

Chats/Texts/IM: Native exports where supported; otherwise, CSV/JSON with fields for sender, recipients, timestamps (UTC), message/thread IDs, and attachments (export attachments in original formats).

Calendars: ICS where possible; or PDF plus any attachments.

Documents/attachments: Original/native formats (DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PDF, etc.).

Logs/Reports: CSV/JSON preferred.

Delivery: Direct electronic transmission via email attachments or open (no login/registration/password) download link hosted by your agency (e.g., SharePoint/OneDrive public link). Please do not use third-party portals that require creating an account or logging in. A single or series of .zip files is acceptable.

If any records cannot be produced in the above formats, please produce them in their native format with associated metadata intact.

METADATA REQUESTED

Where reasonably available, please include customary metadata fields such as: From, To, CC, BCC, Subject, Sent/Received Date-Time (with timezone/UTC), Message-ID, Conversation/Thread-ID, file names, file sizes, hash values (if held), and folder/location paths.

SEARCH DETAILS AND RECORDS PRESERVATION

Please identify the systems searched e.g. (Exchange/Outlook/Office 365, Teams, mobile devices, MDM archives, JustFOIA/CivicPlus admin, helpdesk, file shares) and the custodians.

Please describe the search methods/terms used.

If any potentially responsive sources were not searched or are no longer available, please explain why and what preservation steps were taken.

USE OF THIRD-PARTY PORTALS NOT MANDATORY

Please note that under Washington’s Public Records Act, use of a third-party “portal” is not mandatory for requestors. Agencies may not condition access to records on the creation of an account, the use of a login, or the acceptance of third-party vendor terms.

Third-party portals (such as GovQA, NextRequest, JustFOIA, or similar systems) often:

Require account creation or login credentials;

Restrict downloads, viewing times, or re-access;

Remove or disable links after a limited period;

Place records behind commercial platforms operated by for-profit corporations.

These restrictions unlawfully burden and condition access to public records. The Public Records Act forbids agencies from imposing access barriers beyond those authorized by statute.

RCW 42.56.080(2): An agency “shall not deny a request for identifiable public records solely on the basis that the request is overbroad.” Agencies must provide the “fullest assistance” and “most timely possible action” to requestors.

RCW 42.56.550(1): Courts are directed to liberally construe the PRA to ensure access and strictly construe exemptions against withholding.

Fisher Broadcasting-Seattle TV LLC v. City of Seattle, 180 Wn.2d 515, 528 (2014): Agencies must produce records in a “reasonably usable format when feasible.”

Mechling v. City of Monroe, 152 Wn. App. 830, 841 (2009): PRA is to be liberally construed in favor of disclosure and cannot be restricted by agency practices.

Because of this, I respectfully decline use of any third-party portal. Please provide all responsive records via:

Direct electronic email attachment to this requestor’s address, or a direct, open (no password, no registration required) cloud-based download link hosted by your agency.

Do not register this requestor with, nor direct this requestor to, any third-party commercial portal, including but not limited to FOIAOnline, GovQA (a Granicus Corporation), NextRequest, FOIAExpress, JustFOIA, FOIADirect, or any similar online service.

Do not transmit any portion of this request, or responsive records, to any for-profit vendor or portal. Doing so would unlawfully condition access to public records and contravene both RCW 42.56.080 and RCW 42.56.550.

PUBLIC RECORDS REQUESTS SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL

This public records request is being submitted via email, consistent with Washington’s Public Records Act.

RCW 42.56.080(2) provides in relevant part: “Agencies shall honor requests received in person during an agency’s normal office hours, or by mail or email, for identifiable public records unless exempted by provisions of this chapter. No official format is required for making a records request; however, agencies may recommend that requestors submit requests using an agency-provided form or web page.”

Accordingly:

A request submitted by email is a valid, enforceable method of making a PRA request.

Agencies may recommend, but cannot require, the use of an online portal or official form.

Any refusal to honor this request as submitted would directly conflict with RCW 42.56.080 and the agency’s duty under RCW 42.56.100 to provide the “fullest assistance to requestors” and adopt reasonable rules that do not “unreasonably hinder or delay” access.

Therefore, this request is to be honored and fulfilled by your agency via email, as submitted. Should the agency fail to process this request in compliance with statute, relief will be sought pursuant to RCW 42.56.550 in the form of judicial review, penalties, and attorney’s fees.

INSTALLMENTS AND FEE ESTIMATES

Please provide an initial acknowledgment within five business days (RCW 42.56.520) with a reasonable time estimate for each installment, and

A cost estimate if fees are anticipated (please itemize and explain).

NISSEN AFFIDAVIT AND ALL DEVICE SEARCH REQUIRED

Pursuant to Nissen v. Pierce County, 183 Wn.2d 863 (2015), and its progeny, this request specifically includes all responsive public records contained on personal devices or personal accounts (including personal cell phones, text/SMS/MMS, personal email accounts, cloud storage, instant messaging apps, and social media accounts) of any agency employee, official, or contractor where public business may have been conducted.

To comply with this requirement, please:

Conduct a comprehensive all-device search, including both agency-issued and personally owned devices/accounts used for public business.

Require each potentially responsive custodian to execute a Nissen affidavit or sworn certification affirming:

1. They conducted a diligent search of all personal and agency devices/accounts reasonably likely to contain responsive records;

2. The methods used to conduct the search (e.g., search terms, accounts checked, device types); and

3. Whether any responsive records were located, preserved, and produced.

Produce all responsive records located in such searches along with the executed affidavits.

Failure to obtain and provide sworn Nissen affidavits or equivalent certifications from custodians may constitute an incomplete search in violation of RCW 42.56.520 (requirement for a reasonable and adequate search) and may expose the agency to relief under RCW 42.56.550.

EXEMPTION LOGS 

Please ensure that all redactions or exemptions claimed by your agency in the production of responsive records are accompanied by a complete and detailed exemption log.

Exemptions logs at minimum must contain the following:

1. Identify the valid legal reason (statutory citation) for each exemption;

2. Specify the location of each redaction within the record produced (via footnote, coded reference, or margin notation);

3. State the number of pages or records withheld in their entirety, if any; and

4. Demonstrate that only the minimal exempt portion of any record has been withheld, as required by law.

The Washington Public Records Act requires agencies to justify each withholding or redaction:

RCW 42.56.210(3): “Agency responses refusing, in whole or in part, inspection of any public record shall include a statement of the specific exemption authorizing the withholding of the record (or part) and a brief explanation of how the exemption applies to the record withheld.”

RCW 42.56.210(1): Exemptions must be narrowly construed.

Washington courts have repeatedly enforced this duty:

Rental Housing Ass’n of Puget Sound v. City of Des Moines, 165 Wn.2d 525, 538 (2009): Agencies must provide specific explanations for each exemption; conclusory or vague justifications are insufficient.

Sanders v. State, 169 Wn.2d 827, 845 (2010): “The burden of proof is on the agency to establish that refusal to permit public inspection and copying is in accordance with a statute.”

Resident Action Council v. Seattle Housing Auth., 177 Wn.2d 417, 433 (2013): Agencies must disclose the non-exempt portions of records and cannot withhold more than necessary.

Therefore, I request that your agency provide an itemized exemption log with each installment of records produced, in compliance with RCW 42.56.210(3) and the above case law, ensuring transparency and accountability in the redaction process.

COMMERCIAL PURPOSE DECLARATION

This public records request is not being made for any commercial purpose. The Washington State Public Records Act (PRA) prohibits agencies from disclosing “lists of individuals” for commercial purposes.

RCW 42.56.070(8) states: “This chapter shall not be construed as giving authority to any agency to give, sell, or provide access to lists of individuals requested for commercial purposes….”

Accordingly:

This request does not seek a “list of individuals.”

This request is not made for any commercial purpose.

This declaration satisfies all requirements of RCW 42.56.070(8) regarding prohibitions on lists and commercial purposes.

Warning: The PRA does not authorize agencies to require requestors to complete additional “commercial purpose declarations” when the request does not seek a list of individuals. Such requirements improperly condition access to public records in violation of RCW 42.56.080(2) (requests must be honored by mail or email, no official format required) and RCW 42.56.100 (agencies must provide the fullest assistance to requestors and may not adopt rules that unreasonably hinder or delay access).

Washington courts have consistently rejected agency attempts to impose conditions not found in statute:

Mechling v. City of Monroe, 152 Wn. App. 830, 841 (2009): The PRA is a strongly worded mandate for broad disclosure; agencies cannot erect unauthorized barriers.

SEIU Local 925 v. University of Washington, 193 Wn.2d 860, 875 (2019): The PRA is to be liberally construed to promote access, and exemptions must be narrowly applied.

Therefore, no additional commercial purpose declaration will be completed for this request. Any attempt to impose such a requirement would be an unlawful restriction of rights under RCW 42.56.

PRESERVATION OF PUBLIC RECORDS *** ANTICIPATE LITIGATION *** WAC 44-14-03005 RETENTION OF PUBLIC RECORDS

WAC 44-14-03005 (Retention of Public Records) makes clear that public records are subject to retention schedules, and that unlawful destruction can constitute a crime.

RCW 40.16.010 and RCW 40.16.020 criminalize the unlawful mutilation, destruction, or concealment of public records.

RCW 42.56.100 expressly prohibits an agency from destroying any public record after a public records request has been made for that record, even if the record would otherwise be scheduled for lawful destruction.

In addition, agencies have heightened retention obligations when litigation is reasonably anticipated. Records potentially relevant to actual or anticipated litigation must be preserved until both the public records request and the litigation have been fully resolved.

Legal Consequences of Premature Destruction: In Yacobellis v. City of Bellingham, 55 Wn. App. 706, 780 P.2d 272 (1989), the Court of Appeals held that an agency violates the Public Records Act and is subject to attorneys’ fees and statutory penalties when it destroys responsive records after receiving a public records request.

By contrast, it is not a PRA violation if a record was destroyed prior to the agency’s receipt of a request, provided the destruction was lawful under retention schedules. See Bldg. Indus. Ass’n of Wash. v. McCarthy, 152 Wn. App. 720, 218 P.3d 196 (2009); West v. Dep’t of Natural Resources, 163 Wn. App. 238, 258 P.3d 78 (2011).

Washington courts have emphasized that the Public Records Act (RCW 42.56) and the state’s records retention laws (RCW 40.14) are separate but complementary. Agencies must comply with both.

Accordingly:

Your agency must preserve all potentially responsive records immediately upon receipt of this request.

No responsive records may be altered, deleted, or destroyed until this request has been fully resolved and any related litigation constraints have been lifted.

Any unlawful destruction of responsive records may expose the agency and its officials to criminal liability (RCW 40.16), civil penalties, and mandatory attorneys’ fees (RCW 42.56.550(4)).

RECORDS INSTALLMENTS - ORDER OF PRODUCTION

If production of responsive records will be completed in multiple installments, production in reverse chronological order is strongly preferred to the extent supported by native system exports, provided it does not delay the delivery of installments.

DIGITAL COMPRESSION AND FILE MINIMIZATION REQUESTED IN ACCORDANCE WITH RCW 42.56

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.080(2), please provide all responsive electronic records in the fewest number of individual files, preserving native formats wherever possible. Where appropriate, please use free digital compression (.zip or equivalent) to consolidate responsive records into the smallest number of installments for efficiency and economy.

This approach reduces agency burden, promotes prompt disclosure, and minimizes potential costs to the requestor, consistent with the Public Records Act’s directive that agencies provide records in the most “reasonably locatable form” and “fullest assistance to requestors.” See RCW 42.56.100 (agency duty to adopt reasonable rules for providing fullest assistance); RCW 42.56.120(2)(b) (fees must reflect actual costs, not used to discourage access).

Washington courts have consistently held that agencies must facilitate access in a practical, non-burdensome manner. See Fisher Broadcasting-Seattle TV LLC v. City of Seattle, 180 Wn.2d 515, 528 (2014) (agencies must provide records in a usable format when reasonably feasible); Mechling v. City of Monroe, 152 Wn. App. 830, 841 (2009) (PRA is to be liberally construed in favor of disclosure). Producing consolidated, digitally compressed files satisfies these obligations by reducing unnecessary fragmentation and excess per-page charges.

Accordingly, I request that each installment be produced as a single compressed .zip file (or as few as technically necessary), containing all responsive records in native format, to ensure both compliance with RCW 42.56 and an economical calculation of any applicable public records fees.

COMMUNICATION VIA EMAIL

Please send all requests for clarification, status updates, and production of responsive electronic documents via direct email reply.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. We look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Good Luck.
