communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: KING COUNTY DIRECTORS' ASSOCIATION – Board of Directors Meeting(s) Records (2025)
communications.communication:
KING COUNTY DIRECTORS' ASSOCIATION – Board of Directors Meeting(s) Records (2025)

June 08, 2026

via email to: Kristen Deskin, Human Resources Manager and Public Records Officer <kdeskin@kcda.org>

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act [RCW 42.56], I hereby request the following records:

1. Produce copies of all "Records and Writings" of all minutes, complete meeting packets, resolutions, audio or video recordings, executive session logs, and presentations, inclusive, for every meeting of the KCDA Board of Directors for the year 2025, including all records provided to the Board by Executive Directors Bart Powelson or David Mahalko regarding litigation updates, vendor awards, or funding-out contract terminations.

DEFINITION OF RECORDS AND WRITINGS

"RECORDS AND WRITINGS" as defined by RCW 42.56.010(4): any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, and every other means of recording any form of communication or representation including, but not limited to, letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combination thereof, and all papers, maps, magnetic or paper tapes, photographic films and prints, motion picture, film and video recordings, magnetic or punched cards, discs, drums, diskettes, sound recordings, and other documents including existing data compilations from which information may be obtained or translated.

PRODUCTION PROCESSING AND DELIVERY OF ELECTRONIC RECORDS

Please provide all records in their native electronic format. Please do not instead create new records by printing electronic files then scanning and printing the newly scanned prints.

To preserve metadata and ease review, please produce as follows:

Emails: PST (Microsoft Outlook) or MBOX containers.

Chats/Texts/IM: Native exports where supported; otherwise, CSV/JSON with fields for sender, recipients, timestamps (UTC), message/thread IDs, and attachments (export attachments in original formats).

Calendars: ICS where possible; or PDF plus any attachments.

Documents/attachments: Original/native formats (DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PDF, etc.).

Logs/Reports: CSV/JSON preferred.

Delivery: Direct electronic transmission via email attachments or open (no login/registration/password) download link hosted by your agency (e.g., SharePoint/OneDrive public link). Please do not use third-party portals that require creating an account or logging in. A single or series of .zip files is acceptable.

If any records cannot be produced in the above formats, please produce them in their native format with associated metadata intact.

METADATA REQUESTED

Where reasonably available, please include customary metadata fields such as: From, To, CC, BCC, Subject, Sent/Received Date-Time (with timezone/UTC), Message-ID, Conversation/Thread-ID, file names, file sizes, hash values (if held), and folder/location paths.

SEARCH DETAILS AND RECORDS PRESERVATION

Please identify the systems searched e.g. (Exchange/Outlook/Office 365, Teams, mobile devices, MDM archives, JustFOIA/CivicPlus admin, helpdesk, file shares) and the custodians.

Please describe the search methods/terms used.

If any potentially responsive sources were not searched or are no longer available, please explain why and what preservation steps were taken.

USE OF THIRD-PARTY PORTALS NOT MANDATORY

Please note that under Washington’s Public Records Act, use of a third-party “portal” is not mandatory for requestors. Agencies may not condition access to records on the creation of an account, the use of a login, or the acceptance of third-party vendor terms.

Third-party portals (such as GovQA, NextRequest, JustFOIA, or similar systems) often:

Require account creation or login credentials;

Restrict downloads, viewing times, or re-access;

Remove or disable links after a limited period;

Place records behind commercial platforms operated by for-profit corporations.

These restrictions unlawfully burden and condition access to public records. The Public Records Act forbids agencies from imposing access barriers beyond those authorized by statute.

RCW 42.56.080(2): An agency “shall not deny a request for identifiable public records solely on the basis that the request is overbroad.” Agencies must provide the “fullest assistance” and “most timely possible action” to requestors.

RCW 42.56.550(1): Courts are directed to liberally construe the PRA to ensure access and strictly construe exemptions against withholding.

Fisher Broadcasting-Seattle TV LLC v. City of Seattle, 180 Wn.2d 515, 528 (2014): Agencies must produce records in a “reasonably usable format when feasible.”

Mechling v. City of Monroe, 152 Wn. App. 830, 841 (2009): PRA is to be liberally construed in favor of disclosure and cannot be restricted by agency practices.

Because of this, I respectfully decline use of any third-party portal. Please provide all responsive records via:

Direct electronic email attachment to this requestor’s address, or a direct, open (no password, no registration required) cloud-based download link hosted by your agency.

Do not register this requestor with, nor direct this requestor to, any third-party commercial portal, including but not limited to FOIAOnline, GovQA (a Granicus Corporation), NextRequest, FOIAExpress, JustFOIA, FOIADirect, or any similar online service.

Do not transmit any portion of this request, or responsive records, to any for-profit vendor or portal. Doing so would unlawfully condition access to public records and contravene both RCW 42.56.080 and RCW 42.56.550.

PUBLIC RECORDS REQUESTS SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL

This public records request is being submitted via email, consistent with Washington’s Public Records Act.

RCW 42.56.080(2) provides in relevant part: “Agencies shall honor requests received in person during an agency’s normal office hours, or by mail or email, for identifiable public records unless exempted by provisions of this chapter. No official format is required for making a records request; however, agencies may recommend that requestors submit requests using an agency-provided form or web page.”

Accordingly:

A request submitted by email is a valid, enforceable method of making a PRA request.

Agencies may recommend, but cannot require, the use of an online portal or official form.

Any refusal to honor this request as submitted would directly conflict with RCW 42.56.080 and the agency’s duty under RCW 42.56.100 to provide the “fullest assistance to requestors” and adopt reasonable rules that do not “unreasonably hinder or delay” access.

Therefore, this request is to be honored and fulfilled by your agency via email, as submitted. Should the agency fail to process this request in compliance with statute, relief will be sought pursuant to RCW 42.56.550 in the form of judicial review, penalties, and attorney’s fees.

INSTALLMENTS AND FEE ESTIMATES

Please provide an initial acknowledgment within five business days (RCW 42.56.520) with a reasonable time estimate for each installment, and

A cost estimate if fees are anticipated (please itemize and explain).

NISSEN AFFIDAVIT AND ALL DEVICE SEARCH REQUIRED

Pursuant to Nissen v. Pierce County, 183 Wn.2d 863 (2015), and its progeny, this request specifically includes all responsive public records contained on personal devices or personal accounts (including personal cell phones, text/SMS/MMS, personal email accounts, cloud storage, instant messaging apps, and social media accounts) of any agency employee, official, or contractor where public business may have been conducted.

To comply with this requirement, please:

Conduct a comprehensive all-device search, including both agency-issued and personally owned devices/accounts used for public business.

Require each potentially responsive custodian to execute a Nissen affidavit or sworn certification affirming:

1. They conducted a diligent search of all personal and agency devices/accounts reasonably likely to contain responsive records;

2. The methods used to conduct the search (e.g., search terms, accounts checked, device types); and

3. Whether any responsive records were located, preserved, and produced.

Produce all responsive records located in such searches along with the executed affidavits.

Failure to obtain and provide sworn Nissen affidavits or equivalent certifications from custodians may constitute an incomplete search in violation of RCW 42.56.520 (requirement for a reasonable and adequate search) and may expose the agency to relief under RCW 42.56.550.

EXEMPTION LOGS 

Please ensure that all redactions or exemptions claimed by your agency in the production of responsive records are accompanied by a complete and detailed exemption log.

Exemptions logs at minimum must contain the following:

1. Identify the valid legal reason (statutory citation) for each exemption;

2. Specify the location of each redaction within the record produced (via footnote, coded reference, or margin notation);

3. State the number of pages or records withheld in their entirety, if any; and

4. Demonstrate that only the minimal exempt portion of any record has been withheld, as required by law.

The Washington Public Records Act requires agencies to justify each withholding or redaction:

RCW 42.56.210(3): “Agency responses refusing, in whole or in part, inspection of any public record shall include a statement of the specific exemption authorizing the withholding of the record (or part) and a brief explanation of how the exemption applies to the record withheld.”

RCW 42.56.210(1): Exemptions must be narrowly construed.

Washington courts have repeatedly enforced this duty:

Rental Housing Ass’n of Puget Sound v. City of Des Moines, 165 Wn.2d 525, 538 (2009): Agencies must provide specific explanations for each exemption; conclusory or vague justifications are insufficient.

Sanders v. State, 169 Wn.2d 827, 845 (2010): “The burden of proof is on the agency to establish that refusal to permit public inspection and copying is in accordance with a statute.”

Resident Action Council v. Seattle Housing Auth., 177 Wn.2d 417, 433 (2013): Agencies must disclose the non-exempt portions of records and cannot withhold more than necessary.

Therefore, I request that your agency provide an itemized exemption log with each installment of records produced, in compliance with RCW 42.56.210(3) and the above case law, ensuring transparency and accountability in the redaction process.

COMMERCIAL PURPOSE DECLARATION

This public records request is not being made for any commercial purpose. The Washington State Public Records Act (PRA) prohibits agencies from disclosing “lists of individuals” for commercial purposes.

RCW 42.56.070(8) states: “This chapter shall not be construed as giving authority to any agency to give, sell, or provide access to lists of individuals requested for commercial purposes….”

Accordingly:

This request does not seek a “list of individuals.”

This request is not made for any commercial purpose.

This declaration satisfies all requirements of RCW 42.56.070(8) regarding prohibitions on lists and commercial purposes.

Warning: The PRA does not authorize agencies to require requestors to complete additional “commercial purpose declarations” when the request does not seek a list of individuals. Such requirements improperly condition access to public records in violation of RCW 42.56.080(2) (requests must be honored by mail or email, no official format required) and RCW 42.56.100 (agencies must provide the fullest assistance to requestors and may not adopt rules that unreasonably hinder or delay access).

Washington courts have consistently rejected agency attempts to impose conditions not found in statute:

Mechling v. City of Monroe, 152 Wn. App. 830, 841 (2009): The PRA is a strongly worded mandate for broad disclosure; agencies cannot erect unauthorized barriers.

SEIU Local 925 v. University of Washington, 193 Wn.2d 860, 875 (2019): The PRA is to be liberally construed to promote access, and exemptions must be narrowly applied.

Therefore, no additional commercial purpose declaration will be completed for this request. Any attempt to impose such a requirement would be an unlawful restriction of rights under RCW 42.56.

PRESERVATION OF PUBLIC RECORDS *** ANTICIPATE LITIGATION *** WAC 44-14-03005 RETENTION OF PUBLIC RECORDS

WAC 44-14-03005 (Retention of Public Records) makes clear that public records are subject to retention schedules, and that unlawful destruction can constitute a crime.

RCW 40.16.010 and RCW 40.16.020 criminalize the unlawful mutilation, destruction, or concealment of public records.

RCW 42.56.100 expressly prohibits an agency from destroying any public record after a public records request has been made for that record, even if the record would otherwise be scheduled for lawful destruction.

In addition, agencies have heightened retention obligations when litigation is reasonably anticipated. Records potentially relevant to actual or anticipated litigation must be preserved until both the public records request and the litigation have been fully resolved.

Legal Consequences of Premature Destruction: In Yacobellis v. City of Bellingham, 55 Wn. App. 706, 780 P.2d 272 (1989), the Court of Appeals held that an agency violates the Public Records Act and is subject to attorneys’ fees and statutory penalties when it destroys responsive records after receiving a public records request.

By contrast, it is not a PRA violation if a record was destroyed prior to the agency’s receipt of a request, provided the destruction was lawful under retention schedules. See Bldg. Indus. Ass’n of Wash. v. McCarthy, 152 Wn. App. 720, 218 P.3d 196 (2009); West v. Dep’t of Natural Resources, 163 Wn. App. 238, 258 P.3d 78 (2011).

Washington courts have emphasized that the Public Records Act (RCW 42.56) and the state’s records retention laws (RCW 40.14) are separate but complementary. Agencies must comply with both.

Accordingly:

Your agency must preserve all potentially responsive records immediately upon receipt of this request.

No responsive records may be altered, deleted, or destroyed until this request has been fully resolved and any related litigation constraints have been lifted.

Any unlawful destruction of responsive records may expose the agency and its officials to criminal liability (RCW 40.16), civil penalties, and mandatory attorneys’ fees (RCW 42.56.550(4)).

RECORDS INSTALLMENTS - ORDER OF PRODUCTION

If production of responsive records will be completed in multiple installments, production in reverse chronological order is strongly preferred to the extent supported by native system exports, provided it does not delay the delivery of installments.

DIGITAL COMPRESSION AND FILE MINIMIZATION REQUESTED IN ACCORDANCE WITH RCW 42.56

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.080(2), please provide all responsive electronic records in the fewest number of individual files, preserving native formats wherever possible. Where appropriate, please use free digital compression (.zip or equivalent) to consolidate responsive records into the smallest number of installments for efficiency and economy.

This approach reduces agency burden, promotes prompt disclosure, and minimizes potential costs to the requestor, consistent with the Public Records Act’s directive that agencies provide records in the most “reasonably locatable form” and “fullest assistance to requestors.” See RCW 42.56.100 (agency duty to adopt reasonable rules for providing fullest assistance); RCW 42.56.120(2)(b) (fees must reflect actual costs, not used to discourage access).

Washington courts have consistently held that agencies must facilitate access in a practical, non-burdensome manner. See Fisher Broadcasting-Seattle TV LLC v. City of Seattle, 180 Wn.2d 515, 528 (2014) (agencies must provide records in a usable format when reasonably feasible); Mechling v. City of Monroe, 152 Wn. App. 830, 841 (2009) (PRA is to be liberally construed in favor of disclosure). Producing consolidated, digitally compressed files satisfies these obligations by reducing unnecessary fragmentation and excess per-page charges.

Accordingly, I request that each installment be produced as a single compressed .zip file (or as few as technically necessary), containing all responsive records in native format, to ensure both compliance with RCW 42.56 and an economical calculation of any applicable public records fees.

COMMUNICATION VIA EMAIL

Please send all requests for clarification, status updates, and production of responsive electronic documents via direct email reply.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. We look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Good Luck.

RE: Response to Clarification Request, Board of Directors Meeting Records for 2022, request of June 4, 2026

Ms. Bradford,

This responds to KCDA's July 12 clarification request. The request seeks two categories of records, both limited to calendar year 2022.

First, the enumerated meeting record categories: all minutes, complete meeting packets, resolutions, audio or video recordings, executive session logs, and presentations, for every meeting of the KCDA Board of Directors. Complete meeting packets means the full set of materials distributed to board members for each meeting, including every attachment, report, and exhibit distributed with the packet.

Second, all records provided to the Board by Executive Directors Bart Powelson or David Mahalko regarding litigation updates, vendor awards, or funding-out contract terminations, in whatever form those records exist. If such a record was provided to the Board by email, the transmitting email and its attachments are responsive records.

Third, within both categories above, RECORDS AND WRITINGS carries the full definition stated in the original public records request, as defined by RCW 42.56.010(4): any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, and every other means of recording any form of communication or representation including, but not limited to, letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combination thereof, and all papers, maps, magnetic or paper tapes, photographic films and prints, motion picture, film and video recordings, magnetic or punched cards, discs, drums, diskettes, sound recordings, and other documents including existing data compilations from which information may be obtained or translated. A record falling within either category above is responsive regardless of its medium, form, or storage format, and no such record may be excluded on the ground that it is a recording, a note, an electronic file, or a data compilation rather than a paper document.

To be clear as to the question KCDA asked: the clarification KCDA seeks concerns subject matter, and the answer is that the request does not seek KCDA's general electronic correspondence beyond the records described above. The definition above concerns form, and no record within the two categories described above is outside the request because of its form.

With scope now confirmed, please note the enumerated categories are discrete records for a closed calendar year, maintained in the ordinary course of business. KCDA's July 10 first installment contained two records, the August and October 2022 minutes. Please state, as an actual calendar date, when KCDA will produce the remaining 2022 minutes, meeting packets, and resolutions, and provide the installment schedule for the balance of the request.

My June 29 and July 10 requests regarding fees also stand. If KCDA anticipates any charge for any future installment, please provide, pursuant to RCW 42.56.120(2)(f) and before any copies are made, a summary of the applicable charges, stating the fee schedule relied upon, the per unit rate, the units counted, and the total estimated fee, so that I may revise the request to reduce any charges.

If no audio or video recordings exist for any 2022 board meeting, or if no executive session logs exist, please say so plainly rather than leaving those categories unaddressed.

Nothing in this correspondence waives, limits, or releases any right or remedy.

Thank you

RE: Installment Claimed, Delivery Not Accessible, [request title], request of [date]

Ms. Bradford,

This responds to KCDA's installment notice on the above request.

First, I am claiming this installment now, in writing, effective the date of this email. This request is not abandoned and will not be abandoned.

Second, the installment has not been made available. The link KCDA provided resolves to a Foster Garvey ShareFile page that requires identification and account credentials before any record can be viewed or downloaded. My request instructed, and the acknowledgment did not object, that records be delivered by direct email attachment or by an open agency hosted link requiring no login, no registration, no password, and no acceptance of third party vendor terms. ShareFile is a commercial third party platform, and conditioning access to public records on supplying identification to it is a condition the Public Records Act does not authorize. RCW 42.56.080. I have preserved a record of the access screen the link presents.

Third, the thirty day claim or review period presupposes that the agency has made the records available. RCW 42.56.120(4); WAC 44-14-04005. Records behind a credential wall have not been made available, and no claim or review period can run while access is conditioned on registration with a third party vendor. Any expiration of the link changes nothing, since the obligation to provide access rests with KCDA, not with the link's timer.

Accordingly, please re-deliver this installment by either of the two methods stated in the request: direct email attachment, or an open link requiring no identification, account, login, or password. Please confirm in writing, within five business days, that KCDA will re-deliver in an accessible form, that KCDA will not treat this request or any part of it as abandoned, and that the next installment remains due by September 15, 2026.

If KCDA takes the position that it will deliver only through ShareFile, please state that position plainly in writing, together with the statutory authority for conditioning access on identification to a third party vendor.

Nothing in this correspondence waives, limits, or releases any right or remedy.

Thank you

title: FWS SpaceX Florida

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FWS SpaceX Florida
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents in the possession of the Fish and Wildlife Service Florida state office (or its relevant field offices) that describe plans by SpaceX to build launch facilities in Florida or other infrastructure in Florida. This request also seeks records that contain any FWS determinations concerning the impact of such facilities or infrastructure on listed specie in Florida.  This request seeks records in the possession of FWS between January 1, 2025 to the present. I am a reporter for Public Domain and other news outlets and seek a fee waiver. If my fee waiver is denied I am willing to pay up to $25 for records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jimmy Tobias

communications.subject: Request Acknowledgement - AF 2027-00235-F
communications.communication:
Dear Jimmy Tobias, 
This is to acknowledge receipt of a referral of information related to your May 18, 2026, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request related to a Department of the Interior FOIA request.  During processing DOI located records which were referred to this office for review and response. Based on our initial review, we believe we cannot process your request within the statutory 20 workdays because our organization has a significant number of pending FOIA requests.  To ensure all requesters are properly served in the order their requests were received, we have instituted multitrack processing of requests.  Based on the information you provided, we have placed your request in the complex track. The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) provides for the collection of fees based on the costs of processing a FOIA request and your fee category.  Based upon the information provided in your request, we have placed you in the Private Individual category. We have assigned number 2027-00235-F to identify your request; should you need to contact us about your request.  Please direct your questions to the HAF FOIA team at SAF.AA.HAF.FOIA.Workflow@us.af.mil and use this assigned number to assist us in responding more promptly. We will strive to provide an update between 90 and 120 days.  Our policy is to process requests within their respective tracks in the order in which they were received in accordance with 32 CFR, Part 286.8.  We will notify you in writing if additional processing time is required.  We do process each FOIA request as quickly as possible, however delayed responses can be expected. Very Respectfully, SAF/AAGI FOIA TEAM Government Information Management Branch (SAF/AAGI) Office of the Secretary of the Air Force 1000 Air Force Pentagon Washington, DC 20330-1000

title: Third-Party-Owned Flock Hardware (Savannah City Clerk)

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Third-Party-Owned Flock Hardware (Savannah City Clerk)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any contract, master services agreement, memorandum of understanding or agreement, interlocal or intergovernmental agreement, grant agreement, nondisclosure agreement, or similar document between the Savannah Police Department and any of the following that concerns Flock Safety cameras, solar panels, mounting or power equipment, or other Flock hardware: (a) the Savannah Area Regional Intelligence Center (SARIC); (b) the Georgia Information Sharing and Analysis Center (GISAC); (c) any High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) program; (d) the Georgia Bureau of Investigation or any other regional intelligence center, fusion center, or task force; or (e) any agency, institution, or private party other than the City of Savannah and Flock Safety.
Existing records, such as asset inventories, purchase orders, invoices, grant award documents, installation or deployment records, or hardware lists from the Department's Flock account, sufficient to identify any Flock camera, solar panel, or other Flock hardware used by the Department that is owned, funded, leased, or installed by an entity other than the City of Savannah, including that entity's name.

This request includes responsive records that Flock Safety or another private contractor maintains on the City's behalf. See O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(a)(2)(B). If any responsive record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify the specific legal authority by Code section, subsection, and paragraph, as § 50-18-71(d) provides, and produce all reasonably segregable portions.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

communications.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #FDA-FOIA-2026-1307-CDER-1
communications.communication:
Dear Murdock News,

Thank you for reaching out regarding your FOIA 2026-1307.

Your request has been assigned to our Complex processing track due to the scope and nature of the records involved.  FOIAs are processed in the order in which they were received (FIFO-first in-first-out).  Complex track requests typically require 30 months or more for processing, as they involve locating relevant documents across multiple databases and files, organizing, and compiling extensive records , and conducting thorough reviews for disclosure in accordance with FOIA laws and regulations.  The time until completion depends on complexity of your request,  the complexity of the requests ahead of yours.

CDER can process your request on the Simple track and provide you with meeting minutes discussing trial design, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and endpoints between 2014-2017 for the approval of Orilissa (elagolix) for endometriosis, in full satisfaction of your request within 30 days or sooner. Please note, no Advisory Committee meeting was held for Orilissa, therefore we have no Advisory Committee meeting records to provide to you.  This option would significantly reduce processing time. Please indicate if you are willing to accept Simple track processing or if you wish to maintain the request for Complex track processing as originally submitted.

Please notify me by June 24, 2026.  If we do not receive a response by this date, we will presume you are no longer interested and close this request accordingly.

Sincerely,
Ola Chen
Consumer Safety Officer
Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
Phone: 301-796-3488

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: (WA ESD 123) All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com)
exchanged with any district email account, alias, or internal
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient,
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's
available archival retention window.

TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.

LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals,
and generalized policy or administrative discussions.

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions
may be withheld.

MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5)
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act (O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70 et seq.), I hereby request the following records held by the City of Dunwoody and the Dunwoody Police Department from January 2023 to the present:

Any contract, agreement, memorandum of understanding, statement of work, order form, quote, proposal, or terms of service between the City of Dunwoody (or the Dunwoody Police Department) and Clearview AI, Inc.
Any purchase order, invoice, receipt, payment record, or budget line item reflecting payment to or a financial relationship with Clearview AI, Inc.
Any contract, agreement, memorandum of understanding, statement of work, order form, terms of service, or trial or evaluation agreement under which the City of Dunwoody or the Dunwoody Police Department has acquired, accessed, tested, or used any facial recognition product or service, from any vendor.
Any record documenting access to a facial recognition product or service obtained through a cooperative purchasing vehicle, a state or regional fusion center, a mutual aid or information sharing arrangement, or another agency's account.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

title: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Anne Arundel County Police Department)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Anne Arundel County Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I am hereby requesting access to the records listed below and held by the Anne Arundel County Police Department.

1)	Any policies, procedures, protocols, and/or written guidance for the use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) by Anne Arundel County Police Department. This request includes, but is not limited to policies setting forth permitted and prohibited uses for ALPRs and rules regarding who may and may not use this technology.

2)	Information about which people and agencies have access to images, videos, and raw data sets generated by ALPR systems monitored or maintained by Anne Arundel County Police Department, under what circumstances these individuals have access to the above-mentioned data, and what information must be entered about any data requests. The list of agencies includes, but is not limited to, parking and traffic enforcement agencies, and other law enforcement agencies.

3)	Policies, procedures and information regarding Anne Arundel County Police Department data retention and data purging practices for ALPR systems, including  Anne Arundel County Police Department policies regarding handling images, videos, and raw data sets.

4)	Information about Anne Arundel County Police Department audits or other procedures used to assure compliance with the above requirements.

5)	Information regarding the training that Anne Arundel County Police Department personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

6)	ALPR training materials provided to Anne Arundel County Police Department.

7)	Product and user manuals for all ALPR software and hardware possessed or used by Anne Arundel County Police Department.

8)	The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Anne Arundel County Police Department or by third party who make the information available to Anne Arundel County Police Department. Hardware includes fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile devices. Software systems include optical character recognition and artificial intelligence capabilities.

9)	Description of how targets (aka “hot lists”) are shared with ALPR systems and monitored, including the sources for these data feeds.

10)	A list and map of locations where fixed-location ALPRs are currently located within Anne Arundel County Police Department’s jurisdiction.

11)	The number of ALPR devices operated by the agency for the following categories: fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile ALPRs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, please disclose total charges in advance of fulfilling the request. Alternatively, please consider waiving any fees, pursuant to § 4-206(e)(2)(ii) of the General Provisions Article, as this request is on behalf of individuals served by the Maryland Office of the Public Defender, a state government agency, which solely serves indigent citizens of Maryland. As a result, my request for the above-listed public records is in the public interest. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Gilleran
Chief Attorney
Forensics Division
Office of the Public Defender
6 St. Paul St., Suite 1508
Baltimore, MD 21202
(410) 804-7107
jeffrey.gilleran@maryland.gov

communications.subject: Request for Records, CM 245525
communications.communication:
Good morning,

This correspondence responds to your request for public record(s).
Your request has been evaluated in accordance with the Maryland Public
Information Act, Annotated Code of Maryland, General Provisions Article §
4-101, et seq. (MPIA). Specifically, you requested information and records
pertaining to FLOCK and the Department's Automated License Plate Reader
(ALPR) camera program.

Review of the requested audit logs for the period of July 1 to August 5,
2026 determined that the responsive records entirely contain information
gathered by the automatic license plate reader system. This information is
not subject to disclosure under the Maryland Public Information Act.
Therefore any data request for this information/these records is denied in
accordance with MD Public Safety Code § 3-509(d) and MPIA §
4-326.  Further, MPIA does not require an Agency to create a record
specifically to respond to requests made under the statute. However, I have
attached the Department's License Plate Reader (LPR) Program Reports
conducted to date as this anonymized data may suffice your needs. Please
note that we began using FLOCK in October 2024, therefore, report data
prior to that time does not refer to FLOCK data or use.

The Department currently has stationary cameras placed at 91 strategically
selected public locations. Locations are chosen based on several factors to
prevent crime and enhance investigative and emergency response
capabilities. Disclosing those locations would compromise the efficacy of
those systems, reveal vulnerabilities, and expose surveillance and
operational plans. Motivated individuals could use this information to
exploit blind spots or areas where cameras do not exist. Persons may be
encouraged to commit crimes in unmonitored areas, endangering the life or
physical safety of others and interfering with a valid and proper law
enforcement proceeding. Denial of this portion of your request is in
accordance with MPIA § 4-351(a)(3), § 4-351(b)(1)(7), and § 4-352(1).

I have attached the requested audit reports and the Department's policy
which includes the details you mentioned in your request.

I have also attached the policy regarding this program. In accordance with
this policy, no external Agencies have or may access our data.
Additionally, please note that most Department rules/policies are posted
publicly at
https://www.aacounty.org/police-department/about-us/rules-and-regulations if
you wish to review or further search the Department's policies.

Please note that the statement of work, contracts, vendor information, and
related records are in the custody of the County's Purchasing Office; seek
them directly from that office. However, I have copied the Department's
Custodian of Records so they are aware of your inquiry. There are no data
sharing agreements or memorandums of understanding.

For more public information about the ALPR program, please visit
https://www.aacounty.org/police-department/real-time-information-center/automated-license-plate-reader-program.
Please feel free to contact me if you have questions/concerns about this
response. Pursuant to MPIA § 4-362, you are entitled to seek judicial
review of this response. You may also refer any concerns about this
response to the Public Access Ombudsman. If the Ombudsman is unable to
resolve the matter, you may subsequently seek a resolution from the Public
Information Act Compliance Board for those matters within the Compliance
Board’s jurisdiction. See MPIA §§ 4-1A-01 et seq. and MPIA §§ 4-1B-01 et
seq.
Best Regards,

Katrina Smith #4241
MAII, PIA Manager
Anne Arundel County Police Department
Central Records
410-222-8783
p94241@aacounty.org

title: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Kenilworth Nj Police Department)

communications.subject: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Kenilworth Nj Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Jersey Open Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

For the period July 20, 2026 through August 19, 2026, please provide:

1. Records showing the total number of license plates, vehicle detections, or plate reads captured or scanned through Flock Safety ALPR systems accessible to or operated by the department.

2. The names of all hot lists, watch lists, alert lists, or similar lists used, enabled, or accessible through the department’s Flock Safety system.

3. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities with which the department shares Flock Safety ALPR data.

4. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities from which the department receives or has access to Flock Safety ALPR data.

5. All agreements, memoranda of understanding, contracts, arrangements, or other records concerning access to Flock Safety cameras, systems, or data owned, funded, or operated by homeowner associations, private businesses, private organizations, or individuals.

6. All current contracts, memoranda of understanding, agreements, amendments, renewals, statements of work, or similar agreements between the department, municipality, or other applicable public entity and Flock Safety.

7. All procurement records related to Flock Safety, including purchase orders, invoices, bids, quotes, proposals, requisitions, payment records, and records reflecting the purchase, lease, subscription, acquisition, installation, or renewal of Flock Safety equipment or services.

8. All audit logs, search logs, query logs, usage reports, or similar records relating to the department’s use of Flock Safety ALPR systems during the requested period, including but not limited to:

- Records of license plate or vehicle searches performed by agency personnel;
- Dates and timestamps of searches;
- User identification associated with searches, including names, badge numbers, usernames, or user IDs, where maintained;
- Case numbers, incident numbers, investigation references, reasons, or purposes associated with searches, where maintained;
- Records showing networks or agencies whose Flock data is shared with or accessible to the department;
- Records showing networks or agencies to which the department shares its Flock data;
- Event logs, system activity logs, or audit records reflecting changes to hot lists, watch lists, alerts, users, permissions, or network-sharing settings;
- Records showing changes to data-sharing relationships or network access; and
- Records reflecting live-stream, live-view, camera access, or similar access permissions and configuration settings, if applicable.

This request specifically includes records available through Flock Safety features or reports identified as “Organization Audit,” “Network Audit,” or equivalent audit, usage, sharing, or administrative reports available within the Flock Safety platform, including the “Insights” section where applicable.

9. Records showing the department’s current Flock Safety network-sharing configuration, including which networks, agencies, or organizations share data with the department and which networks, agencies, or organizations receive data from the department.

10. Screenshots, exports, reports, or other existing records reflecting relevant Flock Safety configuration settings, including network-sharing settings and live-stream/live-view access settings, to the extent such records are maintained by the agency.

Please provide responsive records in their original electronic format where reasonably available. For databases, audit logs, search logs, reports, or tabular records, I prefer CSV, XLS/XLSX, or another native machine-readable format rather than PDF printouts.

This request seeks existing government records and does not require the agency to create a new record. If a requested list or summary does not exist as a standalone record, please provide the existing report, export, audit log, configuration record, or other record containing the requested information.

In advance of filing this request, Flock Safety was consulted regarding the availability of these records. Flock Safety indicated that if an agency administrator has difficulty locating relevant audit or system records, the administrator may contact Flock Safety for support.

If any portion of a responsive record is considered exempt from disclosure, please redact only the exempt portion and provide the remainder of the record. Please identify the specific legal basis for each withholding or redaction.

The requested records will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Madthew Pierre-Louis

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the provisions of the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552), I hereby request access to and copies of all records, documents, and communications related to the federal procurement award identified as:

Contract/PIID Number: 70CDCR24FR0000036

Awardee Name: AKIMA GLOBAL SERVICES, LLC

Awarding Agency: U.S. IMMIGRATION AND CUSTOMS ENFORCEMENT

Approved Date: 08/14/2025

Contract/Award Description: HOUSEKEEPING- GUARD

This request is intended to be broad and comprehensive and includes, but is not limited to, the following record types:

All invoices, purchase orders, contracts, loan agreements, and procurement documents (including but not limited to solicitation documents or notices of proposed contracts, proposed bids, unsolicited proposals, and/or documents justifying contracting without full and open competition), statements of work, relating to the aforementioned award.

The final contract award document, including all attachments, exhibits, schedules, and modifications.

The solicitation documents (e.g., Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Quotation (RFQ), Presolicitation Notice).

All proposals, quotes, and submissions received from all offerors in response to the solicitation.

All technical and cost/price evaluations of the proposals, including scoring sheets, consensus reports, and narrative justifications.

The Source Selection Statement and the Source Selection Decision Document.

The Contracting Officer's Final Determination and Finding, and the documentation of responsibility.

All pre-award and post-award correspondence, memoranda, and emails between the agency and the awardee, as well as between the agency and unsuccessful offerors, regarding this procurement action.

All Justification and Approval (J&A) documents for other than full and open competition, if applicable.

All past performance evaluations and records used in the evaluation process.

All internal agency reports, memoranda, briefing slides, and meeting minutes related to the planning, evaluation, and award of this contract.

All documents related to protests, disputes, or inquiries concerning this award, if any.

The abstract of offers (if one was generated).

If any portion of this request is denied, I ask that you justify all deletions by reference to specific exemptions under the FOIA. I also request that you release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of any records. Please provide a Vaughn Index if you withhold information.

This request is for all documents produced between 08/01/2025 and the time this request is processed.

Fee Waiver Request: I request a full waiver of all search, review, and duplication fees. Disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government by revealing how taxpayer funds are being obligated through the federal procurement process. It is not primarily in my commercial interest. I am a journalist with The Latino Newsletter, a new media outlet focused on reporting about Puerto Rico (thelatinonewsletter.org).

If you deny this fee waiver request, I am willing to pay up to $50 in fees. Please inform me if the total fees will exceed this amount before proceeding with processing my request.

Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(E) and 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1)(ii), I respectfully request expedited processing of this request.

There is a compelling need for this information because its disclosure is urgently necessary to inform the public concerning actual or alleged government activity, and it concerns a matter of current exigency to the American public.

The Department of Homeland Security is at the forefront of national issues receiving intense public and legislative scrutiny, including border security, immigration enforcement, and cybersecurity. The award of contract 70CDCR24FR0000036 involves the obligation of substantial public funds for services and capabilities that directly impact these critical DHS missions.

There is a widespread and urgent public desire to understand how DHS is spending taxpayer money, the nature of the services it is procuring, and the companies it is partnering with to execute its vital duties. The release of this information is essential for ensuring government transparency and accountability. Delaying its release would significantly impair the public's ability to engage in a timely and informed manner on these matters of ongoing national debate and current exigency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Carlos Berríos Polanco

Dear Requester: 
This acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), dated 9/7/2025, your request for a waiver 
of all assessable FOIA fees, and your request for expedited treatment. Your request was received in this office on 9/7/2025. Specifically, you have requested records pertaining to Contract/PIID Number: 70CDCR24FR0000036, Awardee Name: AKIMA GLOBAL SERVICES, LLC, Awarding Agency: U.S. IMMIGRATION AND CUSTOMS ENFORCEMENT, Approved Date: 08/14/2025. Seeking all invoices, purchase orders, contracts, loan agreements, and procurement documents (including but not limited to solicitation 
documents or notices of proposed contracts, proposed bids, unsolicited proposals, and/or documents justifying contracting without full and open competition), statements of 
work, relating to the aforementioned award. 
Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA 
regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your 
request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, 
ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you’re able to narrow the scope of your request please contact our office. 
Narrowing the scope may speed up the search process. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 
In addition, ICE acknowledges that your FOIA request includes a request for fee waiver. We will adjudicate this request only if the agency is allowed to assess fees under the FOIA. See 6 C.F.R. § 5.11(c)-(d). If this is the case, you will be notified of our decision in a separate communication. If there are no assessable fees, your 
request for a fee waiver will be moot and you will not receive further communications from ICE regarding fees related to this FOIA request. 
Your request for expedited treatment is hereby denied. 
Under the DHS FOIA regulations, expedited processing of a FOIA request is warranted if the request involves “circumstances in which the lack of expedited treatment could 
reasonably be expected to pose an imminent threat to the life or physical safety of an individual,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1)(i), or “an urgency to inform the public about an actual or 
alleged federal government activity, if made by a person primarily engaged in disseminating information,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(l)(ii).  Requesters seeking expedited processing 
must submit a statement explaining in detail the basis for the request, and that statement must be certified by the requester to be true and correct.  6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(3). 
Your request for expedited processing is denied because you do not qualify for either category under 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1).  You failed to demonstrate a particular urgency to 
inform the public about the government activity involved in the request beyond the public’s right to know about government activity generally.  Your letter was conclusory in 
nature and did not present any facts to justify a grant of expedited processing under the applicable standards. 
If you deem the decision to deny expedited treatment of your request an adverse determination, you have the right to appeal.  Should you wish to do so, you must send your appeal and a copy of this letter, within 90 days of the date of this letter following the procedures outlined in the DHS FOIA regulations at 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(e)(2). You may submit your appeal electronically at GILDFOIAAppeals@ice.dhs.gov or via regular mail to:

Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request.

RE: ICE FOIA Request 2025-ICFO-58843 

Dear Requester: 

This letter is the final response to your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), dated 9/7/2025, in which you requested: records pertaining to Contract/PIID Number: 70CDCR24FR0000036, Awardee Name: AKIMA GLOBAL SERVICES, LLC, Awarding Agency: U.S. IMMIGRATION AND CUSTOMS ENFORCEMENT, Approved Date: 08/14/2025. Seeking all invoices, purchase orders, contracts, loan agreements, and procurement documents (including but not limited to solicitation documents or notices of proposed contracts, proposed 
bids, unsolicited proposals, and/or documents justifying contracting without full and open competition), statements of work, relating to the aforementioned award 

ICE has considered your request under the FOIA, 5 U.S.C. § 552. 

ICE considered the foreseeable harm standard when reviewing the record set and has applied the FOIA exemptions as required by the statute and the Attorney General’s Guidance. 

A search of the ICE Office of Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) for records responsive to your request produced 11 pages that are responsive to your request.  After review of those documents, I have determined portions of 11 pages will be withheld pursuant to Exemptions of the FOIA as described below. 

ICE has applied FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7(C) and, when applicable, 7(F) to protect from disclosure the names, e-mail addresses, and phone numbers of DHS employees, as well as other third-party information contained within the documents. 

FOIA Exemption 6 exempts from disclosure personnel or medical files and similar files the release of which would cause a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.  This requires a balancing of the public’s right to disclosure against the individual’s right to privacy.  The privacy interests of the individuals in the records you have requested outweigh any minimal public interest in disclosure of the information.  Any private interest you may have in that information does not factor into the aforementioned balancing test. 

FOIA Exemption 7(C) protects records or information compiled for law enforcement purposes that could reasonably be expected to constitute an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.  This exemption takes particular note of the strong interests of individuals, whether they are suspects, witnesses, or investigators, in not being unwarrantably associated with alleged criminal activity.  That interest extends to persons who are not only the subjects of the investigation, but those who may have their privacy invaded by having their identities and information about them revealed in connection with an investigation.  Based upon the traditional recognition of strong privacy interest in law enforcement records, categorical withholding of information that identifies third parties in law enforcement records is ordinarily appropriate.  As such, I have determined that the privacy interest in the identities of individuals in the records you have requested clearly outweigh any minimal public interest in disclosure of the information.  Please note that any private interest you may have in that information does not factor into this determination. 

FOIA Exemption 7(F) protects records or information compiled for law enforcement purposes when the disclosure of that information could reasonably be expected to endanger the life or physical safety of any individual.  Please note that, unlike the personal privacy protection afforded by other exemptions of the FOIA, no public interest balancing test is required under Exemption 7(F). 

ICE has applied FOIA Exemption 7(E) to protect from disclosure internal agency case numbers and internal agency URLs contained within the document. 

FOIA Exemption 7(E) protects records compiled for law enforcement purposes, the release of which would disclose techniques and/or procedures for law enforcement investigations or prosecutions or would disclose guidelines for law enforcement investigations or prosecutions if such disclosure could reasonably be expected to risk circumvention of the law.  I have determined that disclosure of certain law enforcement sensitive information contained within the responsive records could reasonably be expected to risk circumvention of the law.  Additionally, the techniques and procedures at issue are not well known to the public. 

You have the right to appeal the above withholding determination. Should you wish to do so, you must send your appeal and a copy of this letter, within 90 days of the date of this letter following the procedures outlined in the DHS FOIA regulations at 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.8. You may submit your appeal through the SecureRelease Portal (preferred) or via regular mail to:

Dear FOIA Appeals Officer:

Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A) and 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.8, I am writing to appeal the response of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement ("ICE"), dated in the above-referenced determination, to my FOIA request seeking invoices, purchase orders, contracts, solicitation documents, statements of work, and related procurement records concerning Contract/PIID Number 70CDCR24FR0000036, awarded to Akima Global Services, LLC. I have enclosed a copy of ICE's response letter, reference number 2025-ICFO-58843, with this appeal.

ICE identified 11 pages as responsive and withheld portions of all 11 pages under FOIA Exemptions 6, 7(C), 7(F), and 7(E). I respectfully appeal these withholdings on the following grounds.

1. ICE Has Not Demonstrated Foreseeable Harm as Required by the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016
The FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 requires an agency to withhold information only if it "reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by" an applicable exemption, or if disclosure is prohibited by law. 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A)(i). ICE's response states only in conclusory terms that it "considered the foreseeable harm standard" without explaining what specific harm would result from releasing the withheld material in these particular records. A generalized recitation of the foreseeable harm standard, without a record-specific explanation, does not satisfy the statute. I ask that ICE reprocess the records and articulate, for each category of withheld information, the specific harm that disclosure would cause.

2. Exemptions 6 and 7(C) Have Been Applied More Broadly Than the Privacy Interests at Stake Justify
ICE withheld the names, e-mail addresses, and phone numbers of DHS employees, along with unspecified "other third-party information," under Exemptions 6 and 7(C). Both exemptions require a balancing of individual privacy interests against the public interest in disclosure. There is a substantial public interest here: the requested records concern the expenditure of federal funds under a government contract for immigration detention services, a matter of significant ongoing public concern and congressional oversight. Federal employees acting in their official capacities on a government procurement generally have a diminished privacy interest in their names and work contact information, particularly where that information does not reveal anything about their personal lives. I ask that ICE identify with more specificity what "other third-party information" was withheld and explain why the privacy interest of each category of individual outweighs the public interest in understanding how this contract is being administered.

3. Exemption 7(F) Should Be Applied Only Where a Specific, Articulable Safety Risk Exists
ICE's letter does not explain what information within these 11 pages of contract and procurement records could reasonably be expected to endanger the life or physical safety of any individual. Invoices, purchase orders, and statements of work are administrative and financial in nature. I ask ICE to identify the specific information withheld under Exemption 7(F) and explain the nexus between that information and a genuine safety risk, rather than applying the exemption categorically to law-enforcement-adjacent records.

4. Exemption 7(E) Has Been Applied to Routine Administrative Identifiers
ICE withheld "internal agency case numbers and internal agency URLs" under Exemption 7(E), asserting that these reveal law enforcement techniques or procedures not well known to the public. Internal case numbers and URLs used to track a procurement contract are administrative identifiers, not investigative techniques or procedures within the meaning of Exemption 7(E). I ask ICE to explain specifically how disclosure of a case number or URL associated with a facilities/detention services contract would risk circumvention of the law, or to release this information.

5. ICE Should Confirm It Released All Reasonably Segregable, Non-Exempt Information
The FOIA requires that "any reasonably segregable portion of a record shall be provided" after deletion of exempt portions. 5 U.S.C. § 552(b). Because ICE withheld portions of all 11 responsive pages, I ask ICE to confirm that a line-by-line segregability review was performed for each page and to release any additional non-exempt material, including the substantive contract terms, pricing, deliverables, and statement-of-work content that do not implicate the privacy or law-enforcement-sensitivity concerns described above.

Requested Relief
I respectfully request that ICE, on appeal: (a) reverse or narrow its withholdings under Exemptions 6, 7(C), 7(F), and 7(E) to the extent they were applied categorically rather than to specific, articulated harms; (b) release all reasonably segregable non-exempt information from the 11 responsive pages; and (c) if any withholdings are upheld, provide an index (such as a Vaughn index) describing the nature of the information withheld and the specific exemption and justification relied upon for each redaction.

Thank you for your consideration of this appeal. Please confirm receipt and provide the anticipated timeline for a determination. I can be reached at the contact information provided above if any clarification of this appeal would be helpful.

Sincerely,

Carlos

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Central Intelligence Agency: Mandatory Declassification Request - GEORGIA: INDEPENDENCE DRIVE ACCELERATING - Document ID: DOC_0005424739
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the provisions of Executive Order 13526, Section 3.5, and 32 CFR Part 1908, I am formally requesting a Mandatory Declassification Review for a line-by-line re-review of the remaining redacted portions of the following historically significant Intelligence Memorandum:

Document Title: GEORGIA: INDEPENDENCE DRIVE ACCELERATING

Document Number / Identifier: SOV M 90-20049 (also bearing identifier CIASOV 120-20042-)

Date of Document: 24 April 1990

Prior Release Date: 29 March 2010

Verbatim File Reference: DOC_0005424739.pdf

https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/document/0005424739

1. Scope and Resource Optimization
To ensure an efficient use of Agency resources, I wish to explicitly narrow the scope of this request regarding the administrative and structural markers found on the initial pages. Specifically, the Page 1 redactions—which obscure internal analyst names, contact telephone numbers, or specific internal branch routing details within the Office of Soviet Analysis—are unimportant to this historical inquiry. I am not challenging the continued withholding of those specific administrative and personnel identifiers under Exemption (b)(3).

2. Justification for Line-by-Line Review of Page 5 Redactions
Instead, this request focuses strictly on the substantive text blocks within the memorandum, where it appears the original 2010 review applied the (b)(1) exemption far too broadly to non-sensitive material.

In particular, the partial-sentence redactions occurring on Page 5 deserve a much closer look. These redactions interrupt paragraphs detailing the localized sentiments, political anxieties, and movements of linguistic and ethnic minorities (including local Russians, Abkhazians, and Ossetians) in Tbilisi just prior to the collapse of the Soviet Union.

3. Argument of Historical Obsolescence
Given that this intelligence asset is now 36 years old, the material is subject to the high threshold for continued classification mandated by E.O. 13526. The localized demographic tensions and micro-political assumptions of April 1990 are matters of deep historical record. There is no plausible risk that releasing the specific descriptive text or generic source qualifiers embedded in these paragraphs would cause identifiable or grave damage to the current national security or active foreign relations of the United States.

Therefore, I request that the Agency perform a rigorous line-by-line review of the Page 5 text blocks, isolate any genuinely sensitive data, and release all segregable, non-damaging historical text.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to Section 3.5 of Executive Order 13526 and the implementing regulations of the CIA's Information Management Services, I hereby request a Mandatory Declassification Review (MDR) of the document described below, with particular attention to a line-by-line review of all remaining redactions currently cited under the 25X1 exemption. The document was partially declassified and released on August 28, 2013, but retains numerous redactions — the overwhelming majority of which appear to consist of brief terminal phrases at the conclusion of individual paragraphs.

Document: The Strait of Hormuz: A Vulnerable Lifeline, CIA National Foreign Assessment Center, GC 79-10085, July 1979
CREST Identifier: CIA-RDP09-00438R000100140001-3
Online location: https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/docs/CIA-RDP09-00438R000100140001-3.pdf

I respectfully request that the CIA's Information Management Services:

1. Conduct a line-by-line review of every redaction in document GC 79-10085, applying the current legal standard under E.O. 13526 rather than the original classification determination.
2. For each redaction, prepare a written justification identifying the specific, current national security harm that would result from disclosure — not a categorical invocation of 25X1, but a particularized finding.
3. Apply the presumption of openness mandated by E.O. 13526 Section 1.1(b), resolving any doubt in favor of disclosure.
4. Consult with any relevant foreign government equity holders (particularly Oman and the successor states with equities derived from the government of Iran) to assess whether continued protection is warranted on foreign-relations grounds.
5. Release the document in full, or provide a detailed written explanation for each redaction that survives review, suitable for appeal to the Interagency Security Classification Appeals Panel (ISCAP).

Thank you for the work that the agency does, and for the agency's commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: MDR request for USSR: GORBACHEV ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT RUMORED
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the provisions of Executive Order 13526, Section 3.5, I am formally requesting a Mandatory Declassification Review of the following document:


Document Title: "USSR: Gorbachev Assassination Attempt Rumored" 
Document Number: CIA-RDP91B00874R000100280010-1 
Date of Document: 25 September 1986 
Current Status: Declassified in Part / Sanitized
Located online at: https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/docs/CIA-RDP91B00874R000100280010-1.pdf

Basis for Request and Justification
This document, originally classified as Top Secret , contains extensive redactions citing the 25X1 exemption. I contend that the information withheld no longer meets the standards for classification under Section 1.1 of E.O. 13526 for the following reasons:

Significant Passage of Time (document is nearly 40 years old)
Death of Key Figures (Gorbachev and Shevardnadze, both mentioned in the document, are long dead)
Source Obsolescence (the intelligence "methods" or "human sources" protected by the 25X1 marking in 1986 are highly likely to be inactive, deceased, or already public especially since the USSR no longer exists) 
Historical Interest 

I request that the CIA perform a de novo review of the redacted portions of this document. Specifically, I seek the release of the text currently hidden behind the 25X1 markers on pages 1 and 2, particularly the table detailing "Assassination Attempts on Soviet Leaders Since 1969" which currently obscures specific details of those events.

If you determine that some information must remain classified, I request that you release all reasonably segregable non-classified portions. Thank you for the agency's commitment to transparency and for the commitment to the release of documents of legitimate public interest.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
