title: ICE DRIL Calls - Aurora

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: ICE DRIL Calls - Aurora
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any record of all calls received by the Detainee Reporting Information Line (DRIL) from the Aurora ICE Processing Center (AIPC) between April 1, 2022, and October 14, 2022. 
For help tasking a timely, appropriately scoped searched, please refer to the agency’s response to the request assigned 2019-ICFO-38997, and particularly, the spreadsheets ICE provided in November 2019. https://www.muckrock.com/foi/united-states-of-america-10/dril-requests-by-facility-72957/

Pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e), we hereby request expedited processing, and make the following statements in support under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 U.S.C. 1746: 
1. On October 14, 2022, ICE announced the death of a 39 year-old Nicaraguan asylum seeker detained inside AIPC. 
See: https://www.ice.gov/news/releases/nicaraguan-man-ice-custody-passes-away-colorado-hospital
2. In the wake of this death, Members of Congress, community-based organizations, and legal service providers providing free legal assistance to people inside AIPC called for a timely, independent, and transparent investigation into the circumstances surrounding this death—which marks roughly 60th time ICE has announced an in-custody death since the beginning of 2017. 
See: https://crow.house.gov/media/press-releases/congressman-jason-crow-statement-on-death-at-the-aurora-ice-detention-facility; and https://www.rmian.org/happenings-news/2020/4/14/medically-vulnerable-immigrants-detained-by-ice-in-aurora-colorado-seek-immediate-release-amidst-coronavirus-pandemic
3. ICE subsequently released a Congressionally-required Detainee Death Report indicating that the decedent repeatedly sought and received medical care for an injury to his foot, which progressed to his calf. 
See: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddrMendozaMelvinArielCalero.pdf
4. There has been widespread, international media coverage of this death. 
See, e.g.,: 
1. https://www.9news.com/article/news/community/inadequate-medical-aurora-ice-detention/73-62542eca-cf06-456e-bea3-65ebfae7847e
2. https://www.cpr.org/2022/10/27/colorado-lawmakers-call-for-investigation-into-death-at-aurora-ice-facility/
3. https://www.9news.com/article/news/local/man-nicaragua-dies-aurora-ice-facility/73-f52d0d45-531c-4e17-a361-1376d887e499
4. https://www.9news.com/article/news/community/inadequate-medical-aurora-ice-detention/73-62542eca-cf06-456e-bea3-65ebfae7847e
5. https://www.westword.com/news/nicaraguan-asylum-seeker-dies-in-ice-custody-in-aurora-15252848
6. https://sentinelcolorado.com/news/metro/nicaraguan-asylum-seeker-dies-while-in-custody-at-aurora-geo-detention-center/
7. https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/news/melvin-ariel-calero-mendoza-nicaraguan-father-dies-ice-custody-aurora-facility/
8. https://localnews8.com/cnn-regional/2022/10/21/melvin-ariel-calero-mendoza-nicaraguan-father-of-2-dies-in-ice-custody-at-aurora-facility/
9. https://www.laprensani.com/2022/10/18/nacionales/3056841-migrante-nicaraguense-muere-bajo-custodia-de-ice-en-colorado-estados-unidos
10. https://100noticias.com.ni/migracion/119078-migrante-nicaraguense-fallecido-migracion-eeuu
11. https://www.canal10.com.ni/noticia/piden-justicia-para-nicaraguense-que-murio-bajo-la-custodia-de-una-agencia-federal-de-ee-uu/ 
12. https://www.vostv.com.ni/nacionales/26279-migrante-nica-fallece-bajo-custudia-de-migracion-e/
13. https://nuevaya.com.ni/migrante-nicaraguense-perece-en-un-hospital-de-estados-unidos-tras-ser-capturado-por-la-policia-fronteriza/?fbclid=IwAR2W_05ASHQlVNaR7ENnk0WR9-zKffBp9wB2BdNlTCVxqJASSTp9FxIPntU
14. https://www.cpr.org/2022/11/03/advocates-immigration-customs-enforcement-custody-death/
15. https://sentinelcolorado.com/news/crow-bennet-hickenlooper-aurora-ice-death-should-be-independently-investigated/

We therefore request ICE grant expedited processing and release these records. 

Thank you for your prompt attention and response, 

#DetentionKills Transparency Initiative
Al Otro Lado

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

communications.communication:
01/04/2023Andrew FreeMuckRock News, DEPT MR136863Boston, Massachusetts 02115 RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2023-ICFO-04101        Dear Requester:This acknowledges receipt of your 11/15/2022, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), for any record of all calls received by the Detainee Reporting Information Line (DRIL) from the Aurora ICE Processing Center (AIPC) between April 1, 2022, and October 14, 2022.For help tasking a timely, appropriately scoped searched, please refer to the agency’s response to the request assigned 2019-ICFO-38997, and particularly, the spreadsheets ICE provided in November 2019. https://www.muckrock.com/foi/united-states-of-america-10/dril-requests-by-facility-72957.  Your request was received in this office on 11/15/2022.Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you’re able to narrow the scope of your request please contact our office. Narrowing the scope may speed up the search process. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner.Provisions of the FOIA allow us to recover part of the cost of complying with your request.  We shall charge you for records in accordance with the DHS Interim FOIA regulations as they apply to non-commercial requesters.  As a non-commercial requester, you will be charged 10 cents per page for duplication; the first 100 pages are free, as are the first two hours of search time, after which you will pay the per quarter-hour rate ($4.00 for clerical personnel, $7.00 for professional personnel, $10.25 for managerial personnel) of the searcher.  We will construe the submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued.We have queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request.If you have any questions, please contact FOIA Public Liaison, Marcus Francis at the address above or (866) 633-1182. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448; or facsimile at 202-741-5769.Your request has been assigned reference number 2023-ICFO-04101. Please use this number in future correspondence. Sincerely,ICE FOIA OfficeImmigration and Customs EnforcementFreedom of Information Act Office500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009Washington, D.C. 20536-5009

Breach/misuse incident reports — any records of unauthorized access, misuse investigations, or data breaches involving the system

Marketing/informational materials Flock provided the agency

Council/commission approval records — minutes or agenda items where the system was approved

Number of plates scanned in the last 30 days and the hit rate of how many scans matched a hot list, and whether that data is broken out by list

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request #26-1953
communications.communication:
Hello, 

The redactions and their exemptions don't apply here. 

First, how do you make the leap from a non-applicable federal statute regarding TSA to exempting the information for privileged information? State records law often supersedes federal public records law. How is the information privileged? 

Second, you cited a catch-all-exemption that is discretionary and not mandatory. The information is of public interest as it involves surveillance technology. In all the public records I've filed over surveillance technology, none cited the ability to defeat the technology as justification for not disclosing it.  Again, there is great public interest in what surveillance technology an agency is using on the public. 

Please provide the exempted records for disclosure. Neither exemption will hold up to legal scrutiny. 

Thank you

title: Request For Review Records - 2025 PAC 90928

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Request For Review Records - 2025 PAC 90928
communications.communication:
To the FOIA Officer for Illinois Attorney General:

Pursuant to Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I request the following records:

1. The request for review in 2025 PAC 90928 (Winnebago County Sheriff's Office) as submitted to the Public Access Bureau, including all attachments, such as the original FOIA request and the Winnebago County Sheriff's Office's written denial.

2. All communications between the Public Access Bureau and the Winnebago County Sheriff's Office or its counsel, including the Winnebago County State's Attorney's Office, concerning 2025 PAC 90928, including:
a. the Public Access Bureau's letter forwarding the request for review
b. any request for further information or records under 5 ILCS 140/9.5(c)
c. any written response or answer from the Winnebago County Sheriff's Office
d. any notice of the supplemental response provided to the requester

3. Any closure letter or other written notice by which the Public Access Bureau resolved or closed 2025 PAC 90928.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

If any fees apply, notify me of the estimated cost before charges are incurred. Records should be provided in electronic format, native and with metadata intact.

If any portion of this request is denied, please identify the specific exemption relied upon for each withheld record and provide an index of what is withheld.

A response is required within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

**BACKGROUND**

The Winnebago County Sheriff's Office in Rockford, Illinois uses Flock Safety Automatic License Plate Reader (ALPR) cameras to record imagies on the street including vehicles of people who live in and travel through Winnebago County. Flock Safety's system keeps audit logs of searches of that data, both by the Sheriff's Office's own deputies and by outside agencies with access to Winnebago County's cameras through the Flock Safety network. Those logs were initially how a coalition of Illinois activists was able to shed light upon the problematic nature of ALPR surveillance weapons leading to the national scandal surrounding Flock Group and other companies profiting off of the manufacture of weapons of empire.

When a journalist requested these logs under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act (5 ILCS 140), the Winnebago County Sheriff's Office refused. The journalist appealed to the Public Access Bureau of the Office of the Illinois Attorney General, which opened request for review 2025 PAC 90928. According to the Public Access Counselor's 2025 Annual Report (March 2026, page 16, attached, <https://www.illinoisattorneygeneral.gov/Page-Attachments/FOIAPAC/PAC-ANNUAL-REPORTS/2026PublicAccessCounselorReport.pdf>), the Sheriff's Office reconsidered and released the logs only after a Public Access Bureau attorney forwarded the appeal to it. The report lists gives the case one sentence and does not say why the Sheriff's Office first chose to keep the logs secret.

The system continues to harden against such surface-level inspections of its mechanisms. On December 9, 2025, Flock Safety emailed its police customers under the subject line "What you Need to Know About Recent Online Disclosures," announcing that it would cut back its Network Audit logs. Two days later it confirmed the change in an email titled "Important Update to Flock Audit Logs to Protect Officer Safety & Active Investigations," which told agencies that "Network Audit Logs will no longer include: Officer names, Specific plates searched, Vehicle fingerprint information." Both emails, sent by Flock Safety executive Chris Colwell, were released by the Niles Police Department in response to Illinois Freedom of Information Act request 25-869 (<https://www.muckrock.com/foi/niles-8224/flocksafety-emails-12-2025-niles-police-department-illinois-200389/>). Flock Safety cut back the logs because the public had started reading them. According to Flock Safety's December 11 email, Network Audit logs now show only a search identifier, the searching agency, the date, the timeframe, the number of networks searched, and an offense type or search reason. Officer names and the plates searched are gone, though Flock told agencies "all the details will be preserved with and visible to the originating agency." The agency that ran the search keeps the full record;  the public reading the logs of the area whose cameras were searched, does not. The logs in 2025 PAC 90928 were requested in 2025, likely before these fields were stripped.

Regardless, audit logs were never a real safeguard and we've learned all we need to know. Flock Group Inc. is a private company. It answers to its investors and not to the community members its cameras record, and it decides for itself what its logs contain. The December 2025 changes prove the point: a vendor rewrote the public record of police surveillance with an email to its customers, and no council, court, or community got a say. Section 7(2) of the Illinois Freedom of Information Act (5 ILCS 140/7(2)) treats records held by a contractor performing a governmental function as public records of the public body, but that promise means little when the contractor controls what gets recorded in the first place. Transparency that depends on the goodwill of a surveillance vendor is not accountability. Logs are engineered to create a story of how a system is used. They will not answer whether the system should exist at all. That question belongs to the local communities being watched, and answering it means challenging the escalating state of surveillance imposed unilaterally across a land under the control of empire. The purpose of a system is what it does, and logs are an inherent part of that system. We only need to look at the impacts of these surveillance systems, and the contexts in which they are applied, to understand the true nature of this apparatus.

The Public Access Counselor works inside the Office of the Illinois Attorney General, and the Attorney General answers for how it enforces the Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Public scrutiny of automated license plate readers is at its highest while several Requests for Review for such audit logs sit in the PAC's queue. In the meantime, the Attorney General's own annual report presents the disclosure of Flock ALPR audit logs as a success.

**ATTACHMENTS**

1. Office of the Illinois Attorney General, Public Access Counselor, 2025 Annual Report (March 2026). The summary of 2025 PAC 90928 appears on page 16. Source: <https://www.illinoisattorneygeneral.gov/Page-Attachments/FOIAPAC/PAC-ANNUAL-REPORTS/2026PublicAccessCounselorReport.pdf>

Thank you for your help,
JB_𝗟𝗨𝗖𝗬 𝝦𝝙𝝘𝗦𝝝𝝥𝗦 𝗟𝝙𝝗𝗦

title: Florida Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety audit (Crestview City Police Department)

communications.subject: Florida Sunshine Law Request: Florida Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety audit (Crestview City Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to Florida's Public Records Law (Chapter 119, Florida Statutes), I request the following records:

- Records Related to the Department's Flock Safety System:

// 1. Organization Audit in Flock: The report should include data logged from the period of December 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency.

// 2. Network Audit in Flock: The report should include data logged from the period of December 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization's Flock network by any agency in the Flock System.

// 3. A list of network share settings that include:
3a. Flock networks shared with me
3b. Networks that I'm sharing

// 4. Contract and Agreement Documents:
4a. The complete, executed contract(s) between the Crestview City Police Department and Flock Safety, including all terms and conditions
4b. Service level agreements
4c. Data sharing provisions and agreements with Flock Safety
4d. Privacy disclosure information and policies
4e. Data retention and deletion policies
4f. Third-party data access provisions
4g. All amendments, addendums, or modifications to the original contract

// 5. Internal Use Policy and Accountability Measures:
5a. Policies regarding authorized users and permissible uses of the system
5b. Training requirements for deputies and other personnel
5c. Audit and oversight procedures
5d. Accountability measures for system misuse or unauthorized access
5e. Procedures for conducting searches and queries
5f. Legal justification requirements for searches (warrant requirements, reasonable suspicion standards, etc.)

// 6. Security and Privacy Safeguards:
6a. Authentication requirements (e.g., two-factor authentication policies)
6b. Password policies, including requirements for length, complexity, and rotation
6c. Standards for regular user account access audits and reviews
6d. Cybersecurity vulnerability assessments or security reviews conducted on the Flock Safety system

- Clarification Regarding Requested Records:

To be clear, I am requesting administrative audit logs and configuration settings that document system usage and network sharing arrangements. I am not requesting license plate images, photographs, or personal identifying information of vehicle owners that would be protected under F.S. 316.0777. 

The audit reports contain metadata about system usage (such as when searches occurred and network configuration data), which is distinct from the protected ALPR images and personal data. This administrative data does not reveal surveillance techniques or procedures under F.S. 119.071(2)(d), as it shows that the system was used, not how surveillance operations are conducted. Similarly, these audit logs are not active criminal intelligence or investigative information under F.S. 119.071(2)(c)(1), as they are administrative records about system usage rather than records of specific investigations.

- Accommodation for Partial Exemptions:

If any portion of the audit reports contains information that your department believes is exempt under Florida law, I respectfully request that you provide the records with appropriate redactions of only that specific exempt information, rather than withholding the records in their entirety. Florida's Public Records Law requires that exemptions be narrowly construed, and non-exempt portions of records must be disclosed even when some portions are exempt.

As an alternative, I would be satisfied with the audit reports provided in aggregate form (e.g., total number of searches by date) if that would address any concerns about sensitive information.

- Format and Delivery:

Please provide records in their original electronic, machine-readable format. For example, please provide CSV or spreadsheet files where applicable. Please do not redirect me to your transparency portal.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment or Dropbox link.


Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as Florida law requires. If you believe any portion of the requested records is exempt, please provide a detailed explanation identifying the specific exemption and how it applies to the specific data withheld.

Respectfully,

Kyle Searfoss

communications.subject: RE: Florida Sunshine Law Request #26-144
communications.communication:
Good Morning,

I appreciate the notice that it would take a longer period of time to compile this data, however it has as of September 7th, 2026 been more than 4 months since I have received an update. It is my understanding that despite the recent FDOT memorandum, the City of Crestview will still be operating it's FLOCK camera network. I believe now more than ever that greater transparency will be required as these systems are continuing to be abused across the country. It is my hope that the Crestview City Police Department is committed to transparency, I would therefore like to update my request to cover FLOCK query logs pertaining to the dates of 1 August 2026 - 31 August 2026. I would also like you to include a copy of your current contract with FLOCK, as well as what agencies you allow to access your FLOCK network. 

If you need further clarification on how to access these logs and connected network products, please contact the Okaloosa County Sheriff's Department who has been kind enough to fulfill several FOIA requests in the past regarding FLOCK systems. I look forward to your response and thank you for your time.

Respectfully,

Kyle Searfoss
